title: Add SD subsystem into Zephyr
body:
# SD Subsystem RFC

## Introduction
I would like to implement an abstraction layer for SD host drivers, similar to what exists in Linux, that abstracts the host controller from the SD protocol. This would place all common SD protocol code into one subsystem, and enable SDIO device support as well as standard memory card support, only requiring vendors to implement drivers for their SDHC peripheral.

## Problem description
Although large portions of the SDMMC standard are common between all SD host controllers, the implementation of SDMMC support in Zephyr is currently split between several vendor-specific drivers. This means that each vendor's driver reimplements the SD host specification, and that new features or bugfixes added to one driver will not be present in the others.

## Proposed change
This change will separate the SD host controller logic (which can be vendor specific) from the SD card specification. SD memory cards and SDIO cards will have subsystem APIs exposed to configure and write to them. SD memory cards can still be used as disk devices via a shim disk driver that relies on the SD memory card subsystem. All vendor specific code will exist at the SD host controller level.

The SD subsystem will handle components of SD card communication defined within the specification, including the initialization and configuration of cards.

For example, the required commands for determining if an SD card supports 1.8V signaling would all be handled by the SD subsystem, but the details of sending the commands themselves to the SD card would be handled by the SD host controller driver and the underlying SD peripheral.

# New APIs

## High level API Diagrams

Below is a block diagram of the proposed SD subsystem implementation:
![SD Subsystem Architecture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34665051/155623078-22c53251-6bbd-49d5-8624-ca0d53be3ec8.png)


For reference, here is a block diagram describing the current implementation of SDMMC drivers in Zephyr:
![Current SDMMC Architecture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34665051/155623111-5bfa8fa7-8808-417d-8e8b-fa84af506658.png)


Note that the specifics of the current implementation may vary at the vendor level. The only portion that is shared between all SDMMC drivers is the api they expose, the disk driver API.

## Common SD API
All consumers of SD devices will start by calling `sd_init`, which will query the card to determine if it is a memory card, or SD I/O device. Once `sd_init` is called, the user can use SDMMC or SDIO specific APIs.
The common API exposes the following functions:
- `sd_init`: initialize an SD card when one is present
- `sd_is_card_present`: check if card is physically present in SD slot

The SD common API is fully implemented and tested. The implementation resides in `subsys/sd/sd.c`, and the api is defined in `include/sd/sd.h`


## SDMMC API
The SDMMC API will be implemented within the SD subsystem. The disk driver will consume the SDMMC subsystem api. The SDMMC api will expose the following functions:
- `sdmmc_write_blocks`: write data blocks to SD card
- `sdmmc_read_blocks`: read data blocks from SD card
- `sdmmc_ioctl`: get IO control information for SD card

The SDMMC subsystem API is fully implemented and tested. The implementation resides in `subsys/sd/sdmmc.c`, and the api is defined in `include/sd/sdmmc.h`

See `tests/subsys/sd/sdmmc` for a project using the SD subsystem API, or `drivers/disk/sdmmc_subsys.c` for a disk driver shim using the SD subsystem.

## SDIO API

**Note: This portion of the API is simply a proposal, and may change when the final implementation is designed**

SDIO support will be implemented within the SD subsystem. Drivers wishing to use SDIO devices can manage them by consuming the api exposed by the SD middleware layer, like the disk driver does for SDMMC devices. The proposed SDIO api will contain the following functions:
- `sdio_io_write`: direct I/O write to SDIO card. First register to write to is provided. If a count of more than one is requested, an extended write will be used to write multiple SDIO registers
- `sdio_io_read`: direct I/O read from SD card. First register to read from is provided. If a count of more than one is requested, an extended read will be used to read from multiple SDIO registers
- `sdio_func_enable`: enable SDIO function. Required before sdio_io_write or sdio_io_read can be used with this function.

Note that the SDIO API is not implemented at this time, because there is no infrastructure within Zephyr that would use SDIO devices, limiting testing possibilities.

## SD Host Controller API
SD host controllers will all have vendor specific implementations, but they will expose a common SDHC api that the SD subsystem will consume (an application may consume this API directly, but there is rarely a reason to).
The SDHC api will expose the following functions:
- `sdhc_hw_reset`: reset the host controller state (do not reset the SD card)
- `sdhc_request`: send a command, and optionally data as well, to the SD card
- `sdhc_set_io`: configure clocks, IO voltage level, and bus width for the peripheral. Can also toggle power to the SD card.
- `sdhc_card_present`: check if a card is present in the slot
- `sdhc_execute_tuning`: execute clock tuning, required when using higher clock speeds for cards
- `sdhc_card_busy`: check if card bus is busy
- `sdhc_get_host_props`: get host properties, including maximum clock frequency, host capabilities, and maximum host current.

The SDHC api is fully implemented and tested. Two host controllers have been implemented:
- NXP's USDHC peripheral, in `drivers/sdhc/imx_usdhc.c`
- A generic SPI mode host controller, in `drivers/sdhc/sdhc_spi.c`

See `drivers/sdhc.h` for the SD host controller API definition.

The SD subsystem consumes the SDHC api, but `tests/drivers/sdhc` contains a simple use of the SDHC api that performs the early initialization steps for an SD device.

# Testing
This RFC introduces two new tests:
- `tests/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_api`, which verifies basic API functionality for SD host controller drivers
- `tests/subsys/sd/sdmmc`, which verifies the SD stack is correctly able to initialize SDMMC cards and read/write to them

The stack was primarily tested on the `mimxrt1064_evk`, but has been verified to work on all RT evaluation kits with a USDHC peripheral. It has also been tested using the `lpcxpresso55s69_cpu0` target, to verify the SD SPI mode host driver.


# Future Work

## SDIO support

This subsystem is intended to lay the groundwork for supporting SDIO devices in Zephyr, but the stack is not implemented. A proposed SDIO api has been defined, but implementation of the SDIO stack is currently hindered by available testing methods, since SDIO devices do not expose a common type of device, like a disk, and a vendor specific SDIO driver would need to be implemented to fully test any SDIO stack implementation. As such, the SDIO api is only a proposal, and would likely not be merged with the initial SDMMC subsystem implementation.

## Dynamic loading

In the initial pass of this implementation, all definitions of SD devices will be statically instantiated from the devicetree. However, SD is by design hot pluggable, and dynamically identifying and enumerating SD devices is a future goal of this work. One potential implementation would be to allow each SDIO/SDMMC driver to register an identifier value for the card (for example, the card identification number for SDMMC devices or the function identification tuple in SDIO devices), and a callback function. When a new SD device is identified, the SD subsystem could compare the identifier values for each registered driver, and call the callback of the first matching driver.

# Detailed RFC

## Devicetree example
The devicetree for a board with an SD memory card present on the `SDHC_0` peripheral and SDIO wifi card present on the `SDHC_1` peripheral might look like this:

```
&sdhc0 {
    status = "okay";
    compatible = "vendor,sdhc";
    mmc: mmc {
        compatible = "zephyr,sdmmc-disk";
        status = "okay";
        label = "SDMMC_0";
    };
};

&sdhc1 {
	status = "okay";
	compatible = "vendor, sdhc";
	wifi: sdio {
		compatible = "vendor,wifi";
		status = "okay";
		label = "WIFI_0";
	};
};
```

In this example, the `zepher,sdmmc-disk` driver will implement the disk driver interface defined in `drivers/disk.h`, and would make calls to the SDMMC portion of the SD subsystem. The SD subsystem would in turn use the SDHC api to manage the SD card. The `vendor,wifi` driver would make calls to the SDIO portion of the subsystem, which would then use the SDHC api to manage the SDIO card. The `vendor,sdhc` driver would be vendor specific code implementing a driver conforming to the SDHC api.

The SD subsystem will leverage the same code where possible to manage SDIO and SDMMC devices, but expose two separate APIs, so that the similarities between the SDIO and SDMMC specification can be handled by the same functions.

## Detailed Initialization Flow

The below diagram is intended as a real example of where each portion of the SD host controller api comes into play during the SD initialization sequence.
the flow roughly follows the command sequence sent during a call to `sd_init`, but is primarily intended to provide a concrete example of how the SDHC api is used.

1. Initialize the host controller
2. Check that the card is present
3. Toggle power to the card to clear any old configuration
4. Request all cards on the bus go idle (this resets card state) (`CMD0`)
5. Query the SD card to determine if it is a high capacity card (`CMD8`)
6. Query the SD card to determine if the card supports 1.8V (`ACMD41`)
7. If the card supports 1.8V reduce signaling voltage to 1.8V (`CMD11`)
8. Get the card's identifier (`CMD2`)
9. Set the card's relative address (`CMD3`)
10. Raise the bus width if the card supports it (`ACMD6`)
11. Select the bus timing and tune the bus (`CMD6`)
12. Tune the SD clock if the timing is SDR50 or faster (`CMD19`)

The below diagram relates these steps to SDHC API calls. For more detail on the SD initialization flow, see SD specifications "Part 1: Physical Layer" and "Part A2 SD Host Controller Specification"

![Detailed SD init flow](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34665051/155623164-80cb5156-2998-431c-a13c-50a439016bbe.png)

title: lib: os: cbprintf: Add new options to cbprintf packaging
body:
Extended packaging by adding an option to create a package that does not contain transient strings copied into the package body. When flag `CBPRINTF_PACKAGE_ADD_RW_STR_POS` is passed to packaging (static or runtime), an array of transient string locations is added to the package instead of copying string body. That creates transient package which is valid as long as transient strings are valid but such package can be resolved to self-contained package.

After this change we can identify 3 variants of packages:

* Self-contained (default) - non read-only strings appended to the package. String can be formatted from such package as long as there is access to read-only string locations. Package may contain information where read-only strings are located within the package. That information can be used to convert packet to fully self-contained package.
* Fully self-contained - all strings are appended to the package. String can be formatted from such package without any external data.
* Transient- only arguments are stored. Package contain information where pointers to non read-only strings are located within the package. Optionally, it may contain read-only string location information. String can be formatted from such package as long as non read-only strings are still valid and read-only strings are accessible. Alternatively, package can be converted to self-contained package or fully self-contained if information about read-only string locations is present in the package.

Added function for copying packages (`cbprintf_package_copy()`). It accepts options to append read-write or read-only strings so it can transform more transient package to more self-contain version. Previously added `cbprintf_fsc_package()` is a copying with option to append read-only strings (and read-write strings). When output package is not provided to copying function it just calculates the length of the output package.

Most important, transient package can be created with `CBPRINTF_STATIC_PACKAGE()` (at compile time) so actual format string is not needed in the binary (fyi @dcpleung). It will significantly speed up logging when message contains string pointer arguments.

The usage for logging will be following:
- statically create transient package
- pass transient function to logging function which will first determine self-contain package size, allocate space for it, resolve transient package to self-contain package.

Copied https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/9d277468ac5f5a81d57440c2762c0bb1ec06443d to use it in the test.

title: Setup MPU for memory regions defined into the DT
body:
Let's try this again from scratch.

### What this is about

In #42008 we introduced the `zephyr,memory-region` compatible that can be used in the DT to automate the creation of memory regions in the linker script.

We want now to extend this a bit so that we can also leverage the same compatible to set the MPU attributes for the region.

### The problem and the current situation

Currently the only way for a SoC (or a board) to configure at compile time the MPU regions is to add, in a soc-specific file, the `mpu_config` struct adding static entries for the new regions with the needed attributes (cacheable, non-cacheable, etc...). This exported struct is then read by the MPU driver at boot time and used to properly setup the MPU regions.

See for example [nuvoton_npcx/npcx7/mpu_regions.c](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/arm/nuvoton_npcx/npcx7/mpu_regions.c) or [arm/st_stm32/stm32h7/mpu_regions.c](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/arm/st_stm32/stm32h7/mpu_regions.c) that are derived from the general file for cortex-M [arm/common/cortex_m/arm_mpu_regions.c](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/arm/common/cortex_m/arm_mpu_regions.c).

This is of course creating a lot of duplicate code

### The proposal
With this patch it is now possible to declare the memory regions in the DT and define the MPU attributes for the regions using the `zephyr,memory-region-mpu` property. When this new property is present together with the `zephyr,memory-region` property and a the `zephyr,memory-region` compatible, the `mpu_config` struct is automatically extended at compile-time to host the DT defined regions with the correct MPU attributes.

So for example in the DT we can now have:
```
       sram_cache: memory@20200000 {
                compatible = "mpu-region", "mmio-sram";
                reg = <0x20200000 0x100000>;
                zephyr,memory-region = "SRAM_CACHE";
                zephyr,memory-region-mpu = "REGION_RAM_ATTR";
        };
```

and a new region will be created called `SRAM_CACHE` and this new MPU region will be configured at boot time with the attribute `REGION_RAM_ATTR`.

### Is this mandatory?

No. Each SoC or board can keep using the `mpu_regions.c` file to do as it pleases. Also the nodes that are not using the `zephyr,memory-region-mpu` are not configured in the MPU.

### What is exactly 'zephyr,memory-region-mpu`?

title: Documentation for `console_putchar` function is incorrect
body:
**Describe the bug**

The prototype of the `console_putchar` function, which reads as follows:

```c
/** @brief Output a char to console (buffered).
 *
 *  Puts a character into console output buffer. It will be sent
 *  to a console asynchronously, e.g. using an IRQ handler.
 *
 *  @return <0 on error, otherwise 0.
 */
int console_putchar(char c);
```

States that the `console_putchar` function returns 0 in absence of errors. However, it really returns the output of `tty_write`, the function it calls, which when called outputs the number of written bytes. In this sense, when `console_putchar` runs successfully, it always returns 1.

Therefore, the prototype documentation shall state that the function returns 1 in absence of errors, or it shall be modified to return 0 in absence of errors.

title: code_relocation: Add NOCOPY feature
body:
### Use case of interest:

Some platforms are shipping in parallel to the internal FLASH some other storage / external FLASH (usually a QSPI FLASH) that can be used to execute (XIP) code from.

The content of this external FLASH can usually be written at flash time using proper tools (see for example the case of the external FLASH on the nRF5340DK that can be written at flash time using nrfjprog).

The external FLASH is a nice addition that is extremely useful when a large application code doesn't entirely fit on the internal FLASH so that we could want to move part of it in the auxiliary FLASH to XIP the code from there.

### The problem:

Right now Zephyr doesn't have a formal and generic way to move at build time part of the code to a different memory region.

### The current status:

Zephyr is indeed shipping a `code_relocation` feature but that doesn't entirely match our needs.

When XIP is enabled, the `code_relocation` feature is used in Zephyr to move the selected code (that is to copy `.text` section, to initialize `.data` and zero `.bss`) from FLASH to SRAM at run time and execute code from SRAM.

The relocation is done by a generated snippet of code that is `memcpy()`-ing the right content to the destination region and also using some build-time generated portions of linker script to retrieve start and destination addresses and regions.

### This patch:

This patch is leveraging the `code_relocation` code and adding a `NOCOPY` feature. This feature is using the `code_relocation` feature to dynamically build the linker script snippets but entirely skipping the run-time code relocation so that the code can be XIP-ed from the destination region.

### Example:

Let's say that we have a big file called `huge_file.c` that we want to XIP from the external FLASH that is mapped in an EXTFLASH region.

In this case we should enable `CONFIG_XIP` and `CONFIG_CODE_DATA_RELOCATION` and instruct cmake as follows:
```
  zephyr_code_relocate(src/huge_file.c EXTFLASH_TEXT NOCOPY)
  zephyr_code_relocate(src/huge_file.c SRAM_DATA)
```
this means that:

- The `.text` section of the `huge_file.c` must reside in the EXTFLASH memory region and we do not need to copy the section there because we are going to XIP it (and we assume that the file is going to be placed in the external FLASH at flash time).
- The `.data` section of the `huge_file.c` must still reside in the SRAM memory region.

### TODOs:

It's is desirable to have the possibility to relocate libraries and pre-build files instead of source code files.

title: logging: Prevent multiple arguments evaluation (take 2)
body:
This is another attempt to fix #42050. First attempt (#42165) was reverted (#42609) due to #42608. Test was failing because of increased stack usage after changes in logging. Increased stack usage has been seen in `CONFIG_NO_OPTIMIZATIONS=y` case.

In this take, logging macro path has been changed so that runtime packaging (the one without preprocessor magic and multiple arguments evaluation) is used always when `CONFIG_NO_OPTIMIZATIONS=y` or `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y`. In both cases static packaging is not needed since static packaging is used to get best performance and with those two options enabled it is not a case. Since preprocessor magic is used only when optimization is enabled, compiler handles it correctly, resolving all static values without bloating stack usage.

Additionally, added a test (`tests/subsys/logging/log_stack`) for checking stack usage when logging is used. Test has been used to characterize stack usage for various architectures (it varies a lot) in 4 configurations:
- deferred mode
- deferred mode (no optimization)
- immediate mode
- immediate mode (no optimization)

Test should detect any unexpected stack usage increases in logging area.

Fixes #42050.
Fixed #43016.

title: Repo size - board documentation - large PNGs
body:
A ZIP of the current repo is about 80 MB. This is painful for everyone new to the project, especially those not fortunate enough to have a decent Internet connection, but further for every code drop, fork, etc. Even worse it won't ever go away (files are kept in history and will be checked out, even if removed).

This is mostly attributable to images in the 'documentation' for the boards. Sometimes entirely pointless images, like boards/arm/blackpill_f411ce/doc/img/blackpill-v2.jpg, and this practice is questionable in general: Why can't we expect developers or users to look this up from the original sources, i.e. the manufacturer? (Avoiding the whole 'storing PNGs in a git-repo is rather pointless'-discussion for now).
It is rather wasteful to need to push around and store 64 MBs of images that will most certainly almost never be used to write code or deploy to devices.

Some of these images easily approach 1 MB, most have hundreds of KB for very simple content, and considering that there are and will be quite a lot of boards, the repository will certainly grow further.

I think it is too late to remove all the offending images (rewriting history of such a popular repository would be rather painful I fear), I think there should be at least safeguards implemented to disallow merging more image files, or if really necessary, at least only if they are below a certain size (50kB?) -- preferably they should be vector drawings anyway?

I couldn't find anything in the guidelines, so please consider adding this wherever appropriate and sensitize the maintainers for this issue.

title: [RFC] stm32h7: Enable support for optional/alternate clocks
body:
## TL;DR ##
STM32 clock_control driver update (limited to H7 for now) to provide a way to configure alternate clocks on peripherals that support it:
```
    clocks = <&rcc STM32_CLOCK_BUS_APB2 0x00001000>,  <- Existing, bus driven, "register" clock
             <&rcc STM32_SRC_PLL3_P SPI123_SEL(2)>;   <- Newly added alternate clock (PLL3_P output here)
```
This alternate clock source could be selected in peripheral driver thanks to new `clock_control_configure()` API:
```
	if (IS_ENABLED(STM32_SPI_OPT_CLOCK_SUPPORT) && (cfg->pclk_len > 1)) {
		if (clock_control_configure(DEVICE_DT_GET(STM32_CLOCK_CONTROL_NODE),
					    (clock_control_subsys_t) &cfg->pclken[1],
					    NULL) != 0) {
			LOG_ERR("Could not select alternate SPI source clock");
			return -EIO;
		}
	}
```

## Goal
Aim of this work is to enable the use of an optional clock in a device configuration.
This is particularly required in case of STM32H7 based platform on which device clock configuration is usually based on 2 different clocks (cf #41650)
- A register clock, required for device configuration, usually coming from APB/AHB bus.
- A kernel clock, which will be used to clock the hardware block (and hence is the one driving the device frequency), typically derived from an alternate clck source (PLL output, fixed clock, ..)

Fixes #41650

### Why it worked so far on H7
Device clock configuration used to be functional up to now since clock configuration was set so that APB clk and alternate device clk (the default reset one) were equivalent. 

### Secondary goal
Besides the initial goal, idea was to provide the basis to support equivalent functionalities on onther STM32 series, such as the possibility to provide an alternate clock to a peripheral. For instance, configuring LSE as the LPUART or LPTIM clock, or HSI48 as the USB clock.

## Update of clock_control API (03/14):
 
Reworked to make use of new `clock_control_configure()` API, cf https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/43790

## Implementation options: 

### Alternate clocks bindings
Additional/Alternate clocks could be fixed clocks (HSI, HSE, ..), PLL outputs (PLLX_P/Q/R), sysclock, ....
For all these clocks, I've decided to keep existing RCC device driver as the clock controller. As a consequence, the dt binding used to select a specific clock looks to:
```
	clocks = <&rcc STM32_CLOCK_BUS_APB2 0x00001000>,  <- Existing, bus driven, "register" clock
		 <&rcc STM32_SRC_PLL3_P SPI123_SEL(2)>;   <- Newly added alternate clock (PLL3_P output here)
```
Another way to support this would have been to set up each potential clock source as a clock controler on its own and use the following binding:
```
	clocks = <&rcc STM32_CLOCK_BUS_APB2 0x00001000>,  <- Existing, bus driven, "register" clock
		 <&pll3 pll_p_output SPI123_SEL(2)>;      <- Discarded binding option
```
I've discarded this second option because, to be consistent with the binding, this second option would require to instantiate each potential source clock as a device driver, each one implementing clock_control API. This would have had negative impact on code footprint, which could have been considered ok for STM32H7 series but problematic on "smaller" STM32 series.

### Clock mux bindings
Complete solution requires to find a way to configure clock mux (as per_ck).

First option is to add a dedicated node descibing  the clock mux. Its only property is to configure its clock input
```
&perck {
	clocks = <&rcc STM32_SRC_HSI_KER CKPER_SEL(0)>;
	status = "okay";
};
```
Works fine, main drawback is the cost (~220 bytes of flash)

A much simpler alternative was to add clock configuration directly to the clock consumer end node:
```
	clocks = <&rcc STM32_CLOCK_BUS_APB2 0x00001000>,
		 <&rcc STM32_SRC_HSI_KER CKPER_SEL(0)>,
		 <&rcc STM32_SRC_CKPER SPI123_SEL(4)>;
```
Though, this proposal has 2 main drawbacks:
- If board dts is poorly configured, 2 consumers of the same internal clock (per_ck here) could set conflicting configurations
- This adds complexity on the consumers driver implementation side that should be able to differentiate between all these clocks 

In the end the addition of a clock mux node device felt saner.

### Dependencies
This work is based on:
- ~~https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41585, which contain the preliminary clock_control driver work~~ merged
- ~~New set of `/include/devicetree/clock.h` macros (cf https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/42326)~~ merged
- Dedicated tests provided in `tests/drivers/clock_control/stm32_clock_configuration/stm32h7_devices/`

### Limitations and next steps:
- Only STM32 SPI driver is made aware of this. All STM32 drivers should be updated to take this new clock config into account.
- Extend to other STM32 series. This kernel clock is generally not available on other STM32 series, but most of this work can be reused to support the configuration of alternate peripheral clocks (like HSI on LPUART). This extension would first require a clock_control driver clean up similar to #41585.
- It is not possible today to `clock_off` supplementary clocks as they potentially clocks multiple peripherals (or even the core itself). So, this most likely requires the use of power-domains

title: pm: policy: extend and improve API
body:
This PR contains a series of improvements and additions to the policy API. They can be summarized by:

- Rename "residency" and "app" policy naming to "default" and "custom", respectively. Since Zephyr comes with a policy that takes into account residency times as well as other constraints, the residency naming alone may be misleading. 
- Moved constraints API to policy, renaming it to the policy namespace and with a more descriptive naming, e.g. `pm_policy_state_lock_put`. The constraint API was only used by the policy manager, so it was not useful used alone. New tests have been added that check the behavior of the policy manager when certain states are allowed or not.
- Added a new set of policy APIs to impose maximum latency. This can be useful, for example, if drivers or application need fast response times and do not want to be impacted by certain PM states.
- Multiple cleanups: removed redundant includes, logging, assertions, etc.

title: dts: zynqmp: Add proper DT-based integration of On-Chip Memory
body:
Just as the Xilinx Zynq-7000, the ZynqMP also comes with a 256 kB On-Chip Memory area.

Until now, this memory area is already properly configured for use as DMA memory when the MPU is enabled, but any use of this memory requires the use of raw pointers.

Identical to how the OCM has been integrated for the Zynq-7000, add a declaration for the ZynqMP's OCM to the device tree, so that the existing linker command file will place any data to whose declaration "__ocm_bss_section" or "__ocm_data_section" has been added there. For the OCM's DT node, the Zynq-7000's compatibility identifier "xlnx,zynq-ocm" is re-used, as it also matches the ZynqMP.

Supporting modifications:
* Add a matching 'chosen' entry to the device tree of the target qemu_cortex_r5 which is based on the ZynqMP.
* Remove the distinction between Zynq-7000 and ZynqMP for the GEM Ethernet driver, which until now has already been using the Zynq-7000's OCM as described above, but has been using regular memory on the ZynqMP, causing issues as soon as the MPU is enabled for the respective target.
* Add the "zephyr,ocm" entry added to the devicetree to the list of supported "chosen" entries in the devicetree reference docs.

title: logging: Make v2 the default, deprecate v1 (alternative 2)
body:
Counter proposal to #41739.

Deprecated `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFERRED` and `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_IMMEDIATE`.

Introduced `CONFIG_LOG1` which enables legacy v1 (with cmake warning).

`CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y` and `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_DEFERRED=y` enables v2.

Behavior for various use cases:

Using defaults
===========

If logging was just enabled with `CONFIG_LOG=y` v2 instead of v1 will be used. If out of tree backend is used which does not support v2 API, application will assert when no backend that supports v2 is found. `CONFIG_LOG1=y` can be added to use legacy backend.

Explicitly using v1
==============

If `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_DEFFERED=y` or `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y` was used v2 instead of v1 will be used. If out of tree backend is used which does not support v2 API, application will assert when no backend that supports v2 is found. `CONFIG_LOG1=y` can be added to use legacy backend.

Explicitly using v2
==============

If `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFFERED=y` or `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y` there will be cmake warning but there will be no change in implementation. `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFFERED=y` can be removed since deferred mode is the default one. CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y` shall be changed to `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE=y`.

With this approach, when logging v1 is removed, just `CONFIG_LOG1` is removed.

Fixes #41728.

title: doc: extensions: add kconfig search extension
body:
# Introduction

This PR adds a new Sphinx extension to handle Kconfig documentation. The way this extension works differs significantly from the current approach, mainly due to technical limitations that will be detailed next. As of today, a bunch of RST pages are generated (one per option, so ~10K) by a script (`gen_kconfig_rest.py`). These pages get parsed and rendered by Sphinx when the documentation is built. It turns out that adding ~10K individual pages to Sphinx slows things down, to a point we had to create the `KCONFIG_TURBO_MODE` or `html-fast` targets. In practice, this means that any viable solution needs to stay away from individual pages. In fact, the way bindings docs work suffer from the same issue, just that we still have less of them.

Technical aspects of the solution proposed here:

- It is a native Sphinx extension (no more CMake hackery required)
- It uses `kconfiglib` to build a JSON database for all Kconfig symbols
- Introduces a new Sphinx language domain for Kconfig. The domain provides a Sphinx directive (`.. kconfig:search::`) that can be used to insert a Kconfig search tool on any RST page. When building HTML docs, that directive gets replaced by an actual search form. The `:kconfig:option:` role is now available to reference options (goes to Kconfig search form pre-selecting the option). Thanks to using a regular Sphinx domain, Kconfig options can also be referenced in other projects using Intersphinx.
- A client-side Javascript library takes care of the rest: fetches the database and, based on user input, it renders Kconfig content dynamically. The library also handles URL hash, that is, if the page holding the Kconfig form is queried with `#KCONFIG_OPTION_TO_DISPLAY` it will just display it. This allows for _permalinks_, e.g., [CONFIG_SPI](https://teslabs.github.io/zephyr-kconfig-test/kconfig.html#CONFIG_SPI).

Pros:
- A native Sphinx extension
- Only a single page is needed: this means docs will be faster by default
- We can quickly search Kconfig options (it's faster than Sphinx search!)

Cons:
- Kconfig options don't have a page now, so search engines will not index them.

# Demo

https://teslabs.github.io/zephyr-kconfig-test/kconfig.html

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/153750892-3f84a2d5-a3a3-4e9b-a52e-a037cf2f06ea.png)

title: Deploy generated docs from PRs
body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

Changes affecting the Documentation are often hard to review if you can't browse the final generated HTML pages.

As pointed out by @henrikbrixandersen, the build artifacts can be downloaded. However, this involves some additional steps by the reviewer (click through the GH Actions results, download the file locally, unzip it, browse to the location).

It would be nice to be able to view the updated docs with a single click.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

GitHub pages could be used to deploy the generated docs for each PR.

If they are stored in the `gh-pages` branch in a subfolder `pr/12345`, the website will be accessible under https://zephyrproject-rtos.github.io/zephyr/pr/12345.

**Necessary actions**

1. Enable `gh-pages` feature
2. Add additional GitHub action to deploy docs for PRs

Ideally, a bot would automatically add a link to the rendered docs in the PR.

I'd be willing to create a PR for the GH action workflow.

**Security considerations**

It is a potential security risk to automatically deploy something based on a PR that can be created from anyone on the internet. However, I think in this case the risk is acceptable:

- GitHub pages only allows static websites, so the main risk would be malicious JavaScript code.
- We are not deploying to any official Zephyr website.
- Malicious JavaScript code would have to go through the Doxygen/Sphinx/Breathe chain. Not sure if it's possible to inject JavaScript into the generated websites.
- It seems to be possible to configure certain actions to be manually triggered by a maintainer/collaborator, which could make sense for the final deployment step.

CC @carlescufi @gmarull @nashif

I encountered a problem using the ADC on STM32WL55 where the conversion completion interrupt would not fire. Using `git bisect` I found that there was a regression introduced by commit 58b8c4006e1bc0bb2ee8056b807ecb11e1be71bb.

I found that the ADC had to be disabled when configuring oversampling, and then re-enabled, otherwise some other bits in the ADC_CFGR2 register would reset. This seems to have been partially fixed by 97c031822bf023145e8b54492fc09b41df2fe719, only to regress again at acad37196d1f9bf32e82a8af6f085d6f8eb356aa.

Of all revision mentioned so far 97c031822bf023145e8b54492fc09b41df2fe719 comes the closest to working. I do get conversions but the value is always 0. The sample prints `ADC reading: 0`. Waiting for ADRDY when re-enabling the ADC fixes that, and since this is done at a couple other places I added a wrapper for `LL_ADC_Enable` which includes the wait on ADRDY. 

This PR also adds support for running the ADC sample on nucleo_wl55jc, which is what I've been using to test. If this is undesired I'll break it out into its own PR.

body: **Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.** When documenting external libraries that depend on Zephyr functionality, it is natural to reference Zephyr functions/structs/macros with the Doxygen `@ref` command. For Doxygen to accept these references to an external project, a tagfile must be provided so that Doxygen knows where to find and link the references. ``` TAGFILES = "/home/jordan/zephyr.tag=https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/html/" ``` This then turns `Returned structures must be freed via @ref bt_conn_unref` (in some external project) into ``` Returned structures must be freed via bt_conn_unref ``` Which correctly resolves to: https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/html/group__bt__conn.html#ga4b18c6b22a9f02be0d7d078b2ce51ff6 For this process to work, all that is needed is the `zephyr.tag` file, which can be automatically output by Doxygen. **Describe the solution you'd like** 1. Generate the tag file as part of the standard documentation build (in `zephyr.doxyfile.in`) ``` GENERATE_TAGFILE = some/dir/zephyr.tag ``` 2. Host the tag file on https://docs.zephyrproject.org/, probably somewhere under https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen. This file is currently ~9MB. This would then enable the following workflow in external projects when building docs: ``` configure: wget https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/zephyr.tag -O ~/zephyr.tag cmake \ -GNinja \ -B${BUILDDIR} \ -S. \ -DDOC_TAG=${DOC_TAG} \ -DSPHINXOPTS="${SPHINXOPTS}" \ -DLATEXMKOPTS="${LATEXMKOPTS}" \ -DKCONFIG_TURBO_MODE=${KCONFIG_TURBO_MODE} \ -DZEPHYR_TAG_FILE=~/zephyr.tag ``` **Describe alternatives you've considered** Tag files can be generated by end-users for different Zephyr versions, but this is time-consuming and not guaranteed to result in the same results/mapping as what is online.

title: drivers: can: rename API functions for better consistency
body:
Rename a few CAN API functions for clarity and consistency with other Zephyr RTOS APIs.

- `CAN_DEFINE_MSGQ()` becomes `CAN_MSGQ_DEFINE()` to match `K_MSGQ_DEFINE()`.
- `can_attach_isr()` becomes `can_add_rx_filter()` since a filter callback function is not an interrupt service routine (although it is called in isr context). The word "attach" is replaced with "add" since filters are added, not attached. This matches the terminology used is other Zephyr APIs better.
- `can_detach()` becomes `can_remove_rx_filter()` to pair with `can_add_rx_filter()`.
- `can_attach_msgq()` becomes `can_add_rx_filter_msgq()` and documentation is updated to mention its relationship with `can_add_rx_filter()`.
- `can_register_state_change_isr()` becomes `can_set_state_change_callback()` since a state change callback function is not an interrupt service routine (although it is called in isr context). The word "register" is replaced with "set" since only one state change callback can be in place.

Signed-off-by: Henrik Brix Andersen <hebad@vestas.com>

title: cmake: package_helper CMake script
body:
The Zephyr CMake package helper script allows to invoke Zephyr package
modules as they are invoked at configure time, up to the modules given
with `-DMODULES=<modules>`.
This allows to run the configure time part of the Zephyr build system
without generating a complete build system.

This means that for example devicetree module can be invoked for a given
sample and board to generate zephyr.dts identical to what is created
by the build system during a build.

To generate zephyr.dts for hello_world, invoke the script as:
$ cmake -DBOARD=<board> -B build -S samples/hello_world \
$       -DMODULES=dts -P <ZEPHYR_BASE>/cmake/package_helper.cmake

Other modules, for example 'kconfig' and 'zephyr_modules' can also be
invoked this way.

This will allow other tools, such as twister, to executed only a
subset of the build system like dts in order to do filtering before
determine if a complete build should be invoked.

Signed-off-by: Torsten Rasmussen <Torsten.Rasmussen@nordicsemi.no>

title: Zephyr package modules
body:
This is a complete Zephyr CMake package and CMake modules overhaul.

The intention with this major cleanup is to make the build system more modular in a way so that it can easier be reused through the Zephyr package mechanism.

Use-cases for this work is:
- The sysbuild proposal: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/40555
  In #40555 it will remove the need for a boilerplate file like this: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/641b86999750f1ed71fffda1da7c47387db22c23/sysbuild/cmake/boilerplate.cmake as this can now be handled as part of Zephyr package loading.
- Possibility to run Zephyr CMake configure stages individually, for example dts or kconfig.
  This will allow twister to generate the zephyr.dts tree and do filtering and not invoking a complete CMake configuration.
  This opens for the use-case referenced by @mbolivar-nordic on Discord https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/733037738068148335/914952860192632852
  See a PR for this work: #41302
- Cleanup of `find_package(ZephyrUnittest)` as that can simply be loaded as specific module like: `find_package(Zephyr COMPONENTS unittest)`

With the improved Zephyr CMake package, it is now possible to do:
`find_package(Zephyr)` : Will load a standard build setup as always
`find_package(Zephyr COMPONENTS unittest)`: Load specific unittest build setup
`find_package(Zephyr COMPONENTS dts)`: Load only dts module (and its direct dependencies)
`find_package(Zephyr COMPONENTS extensions west zephyr_module)`: Load specific modules(and their direct dependencies), for example sysbuild use-case/

title: Stress test framework (ztress)
body:
Zephyr stress test framework (Ztress) provides environment for executing user
functions in multiple priority contexts. It can be used to validate that code is
resilient to preemptions. Framework tracks number of executions and preemptions
for each context. Execution can have various completion conditions like timeout,
number of executions or number of preemptions.

Framework is setting up the environment by creating requested number of threads
(each on different priority), optionally starting a timer. For each context, user
function (different for each context) is called and then context sleeps for
randomized amount of system ticks. Framework is tracking CPU load and adjusts sleeping
periods to achieve higher CPU load. In order to increase probability of preemptions,
system clock frequency should be relatively high. Default 100 Hz on QEMU x86
is much too low and it is recommended to increase it to 100 kHz.

Example below presents how to setup and run 3 contexts (one is k_timer interrupt handler
context). Completion criteria is set to at least 10000 executions of each context and
1000 preemptions of the lowest priority context. Additionally, timeout is configured
to complete after 10 seconds if those conditions are not met. Last argument of each
context is initial sleep time which will be adjusted throughout a test to get
highest CPU load.

```
ztress_set_timeout(K_MSEC(10000));
ZTRESS_EXECUTE(ZTRESS_TIMER(foo_0, user_data_0, 10000, Z_TIMEOUT_TICKS(20)),
               ZTRESS_THREAD(foo_1, user_data_1, 10000, 0, Z_TIMEOUT_TICKS(20)),
               ZTRESS_THREAD(foo_2, user_data_2, 10000, 1000, Z_TIMEOUT_TICKS(20)));
```

After test completion report is printed with test details. Example
```
Ztress execution report:
	 context 0:
		 - executed:2341, preempted:0
		 - ticks initial:30, optimized:16
	 context 1:
		 - executed:1000, preempted:881
		 - ticks initial:30, optimized:16
	 context 2:
		 - executed:525, preempted:511
		 - ticks initial:30, optimized:16
	Avarage CPU load:78%, measurements:7
```
It is intended to standardize and replace existing implementations where such stress test was implemented directly in the test. I'm aware of at least 3 such tests:
- ring buffer (i will soon PR changes to ring buffer to use ztress)
-  mpsc_pbuf in #38777
- uart_mix_fifo_poll test suite

The solutions considered have mainly been to have either

When designing the API, we need to keep in mind that 

- Some applications may need to only use e.g. the Volume Control Profile (remote controller for just volume)
- Some applications may need to only use stream control without content control
- Some applications may want to have a very simple interface for using e.g. HAP or TMAP (i.e. very high level APIs)
- A bigger API makes maintenance more expensive/harder

We only need to consider qualification in the APIs.

```
doc: drop single quote references 

Many documents relied on single quotes to create references, e.g.

enabled in Sphinx conf.py. However, this method comes with its problems:

Usages have been found using `git grep '`[^`]*` ' -- **/*.rst`.
```

title: documentation generation fails on function typedefs
body:
**Describe the bug**

The source code parsing tool is having issues with function typedefs.
And here I insist on "function" typedefs as opposed to "function pointer"
typedefs. Something like:

```
typedef bool (npf_test_fn_t)(struct npf_test *test, struct net_pkt *pkt);
```

The result is:

```
Warning, treated as error:
/home/runner/work/zephyr/zephyr/doc/_build/src/reference/networking/net_pkt_filter.rst:92:Type
must be either just a name or a typedef-like declaration.
If just a name:
  Error in declarator or parameters
  Invalid C declaration: Expected identifier in nested name, got keyword: bool [error at 4]
    bool() npf_test_fn_t (struct npf_test *test, struct net_pkt *pkt)
    ----^
If typedef-like declaration:
  Error in declarator
  If declarator-id with parameters:
    Invalid C declaration: Expected identifier in nested name. [error at 4]
      bool() npf_test_fn_t (struct npf_test *test, struct net_pkt *pkt)
      ----^
  If parenthesis in noptr-declarator:
    Error in declarator or parameters
    Invalid C declaration: Expected identifier in nested name. [error at 5]
      bool() npf_test_fn_t (struct npf_test *test, struct net_pkt *pkt)
      -----^
```

As can be seen above, parenthesis are moved to the bool keyword as if that was
a function which is not what the original code does at all.

Moving the typedef to a function pointer does not exhibit such issue:

```
typedef bool (*npf_test_fn_t)(struct npf_test *test, struct net_pkt *pkt);
```

but that is an unacceptable compromise as it makes the code much less
straightforward and enjoyable to work with.

**To Reproduce**

Check out PR #39936 and build the documentation.

Or look at the corresponding CI failure report.

**Expected behavior**

The CI documentation check should pass.

**Impact**

This is preventing PR #39936 from reaching a mergeable state.

title: Docs: devicetree is a configuration language
body:
At some point, the cmake and kconfig pages were moved to a new "Build
and Configuration systems" section, which gets its own entry in the
left hand index on the HTML documentation. However, the devicetree
pages were left where they were.

This is very confusing, because it implies that devicetree is not a
configuration language for the build system, when it definitely is
exactly that. The contents of the devicetree are used to decide what
devices should be allocated within the device model, how they should
be configured at initialization time, what their power management
states are, what their pin control settings should be, and more.

This is clearly a configuration language; the current structure is
misleading at best.

Fix it by moving the devicetree pages under the 'Build and
configuration systems'.

title: pm: device_runtime: API improvements
body:
This PR introduces a few relevant changes:

1. pm: device_runtime: simplify error handling for get/put 

	  In case runtime PM is not enabled (or not built-in), the get/put
	  functions always return 0 (instead of -ENOTSUP/-ENOSYS). When runtime PM
	  is disabled, a device is left into active state. Similarly, when device
	  runtime PM is not built-in, it is safe to assume that a device will
	  be active when it is called. If a user implements a custom solution, it
	  is its responsability to make sure that a device is active when using
	  it. For all these reasons, the -ENOTSUP/-ENOSYS are error codes that
	  should always be ignored by devices using get/put, since in practice it
	  means that: device is active, function is a no-op. The example below
	  illustrates how error handling is simplified:
	  
	  ```c
	  /* before: safe to ignore -ENOSYS/-ENOTSUP since device is active (we
	   * can continue)
	   */
	  ret = pm_device_runtime_get(dev);
	  if ((ret < 0) && (ret != -ENOSYS) && (ret != -ENOTSUP)) {
		  return ret;
	  }
	  
	  /* now */
	  ret = pm_device_runtime_get(dev);
	  if (ret < 0) {
		  return ret;
	  }
	  ```
2. pm: device_runtime: suspend device on enable 

	  The pm_device_runtime_enable did not suspend devices, so it assumed that
	  the device was in a physically suspended state. This change makes sure
	  that device is left in a suspended state if the device is initially
	  active.

3. pm: device_runtime: add pm_device_runtime_init_suspended 

	  By default, device state is initialized to PM_DEVICE_STATE_ACTIVE. In
	  general, this makes sense because the device initialization function
	  will resume and configure a device, leaving it operational. However,
	  when device runtime PM is enabled, the device may not be resumed and the
	  init function will just enable device runtime PM. If that is the case,
	  this function can be used to set the initial device state to
	  PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPENDED.

As a result, the usage of the device runtime PM API has been improved in STM32 GPIO/pinmux drivers.

title: cmake: introduce snippets for common configuration
body:
Introduces the concept of snippet's to application configuration. A snippet is a piece of functionality that is not the default behaviour of a board, but is a common configuration that users may wish to apply.

One example snippet concept is "usb" which may route the console to USB instead of a serial port. Another common snippet could be "mcuboot", which would define the flash partitions required for applications to be loaded by a bootloader.

The name "snippet" was chosen mainly to avoid collisions with existing terms. Alternatives considered include:
 * overlay (collision with devicetree overlay concept)
 * config (collision with Kconfig)
 * fragment (collision with .conf files [Kconfig fragments])
 * part (collision with --pristine build option, flash partitions)
 * layout (implies memory configuration)

The Oxford dictionary definition of snippet appears to match this concept well, "a small piece or brief extract".

Snippets are a required devicetree `.overlay` file and an optional `.conf` file that are appended to the existing CMake variables `DTC_OVERLAY_FILE` and `CONF_FILE`. The initial search paths for these files are `${APPLICATION_SOURCE_DIR}/${BOARD}/snippets` and `${BOARD_DIR}/snippets`, with the application directory having precedence to allow for overriding board defaults.

This is a first step towards #34167, as it enables generating `zephyr.dts` files with only the partitions required by an application.
Related to the Zephyr developer summit talk "Common Application Configuration for boards".

Please keep bike-shedding about the name "snippet" to a minimum, I fully expect this to go to "dev-review" which would decide the name anyway 😄.

title: (Yet Another) Memory Blocks Allocator
body:
This introduces (yet another) memory blocks allocator. This allows memory blocks to be dynamically allocated from a designated memory region, where:

* All memory blocks have a single fixed size.
* Multiple blocks can be allocated or freed at the same time.
* A group of blocks allocated together may not be contiguous. This is useful for operations such as scatter-gather DMA transfers.
* Bookkeeping of allocated blocks is done outside of the associated buffer (unlike memory slab). This allows the buffer to reside in memory regions where these can be powered down to conserve energy.

This also adds wrapper interface similar to `sys_multi_heap` so multiple allocators can be handled as a group.

title: Add note in documentation about disabling mass storage when performing mcumgr serial DFU
body:
**Problem**
When performing an mcumgr serial DFU from Linux to the [smp_svr sample](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/samples/subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_svr) (nRF52840 DK), I encountered issues. Specifically, when executing the command _"mcumgr .. image upload.."_, it stalled at 0%

After several hours of debugging I found a comment in [Zephyr issue 9509 about disabling mass storage](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/9509#issuecomment-437418756) that helped me resolve the issue. After following https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/guides/tools/nordic_segger.html#disabling-the-mass-storage-device-functionality I was able to run the "image upload" command. 

**Solution**
It would be nice if we could add a note in https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/samples/subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_svr/README.html#building-the-sample-application about this, so other developers don't have to go through the same hassle as me. If they're using an nRF board and are performing a serial DFU that goes through the SEGGER debugger, they need to disable mass storage for it to work.

I'm not sure if this is issue a general SEGGER problem, or if it only happens with nrf platforms.

title: soc: arm: xilinx_zynq7000: Re-organize SoC data and init code
body:
Re-organize the Zynq-7000 SoC family/series/model/device tree configuration data so that:

* Board definitions can distinguish between the single-core (XC7ZxxxS)
and dual-core (XC7Zxxx) ARM Cortex-A9 models. Further descriptions
of on-chip resources, in particular relating to the programmable logic
capabilities if support of this functionality is to be implemented,
can be added at a later time.
* Separate SoC initialization code exists for the two series, so that
the init code of the XC7Zxxx series can consider SMP while the init
code of the single-core XC7ZxxxS series doesn't have to.
* Device drivers which don't have to distinguish between the single-
and double-core series of the SoC family can use a common configuration
item whenever the pre-processor is used to enable Zynq-7000-specific
code.
* The "cpus" node is removed from the device tree at SoC level and is moved
to the respective board's device tree instead. This shift prevents the need
to have a separate SoC device tree for the single- and dual-core Zynq models,
as the only difference between those files would be 1 vs. 2 CPU cores. While
the different models within the Zynq-7000 series differ when it comes to I/O
pin count and programmable logic resources, the smaller, single-core XC7ZxxxS
models have exactly the same peripheral feature set as the larger dual-core
XC7Zxxx models.

The following other components are affected by this change:
* Xilinx UART driver
* Xilinx GEM Ethernet driver
* QEMU Cortex-A9 board defconfig & dts files
* Zynq-7000 dts file
The required modifications of these components are contained in this package.

title: doc: restore environment variables page
body:
This was moved into the application development guide in commit
bf9ceac2ef82ddd8b4436d12016d70ffff849bbf
(" doc: move env_vars into application development").

That commit claimed the following rationale:

  No reason why we are duplicating this information in a standalone
  guide when we already talk about env variables in the application
  developer guide.

A github comment later says the duplication was in "Important build
system variables":

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/34364#discussion_r616646517

This is incorrect and a misreading of the application development
guide.

The application development guide is talking about **cmake**
variables. These are not the same thing at all as **environment**
variables; treating them as if they are the same is simply wrong and
misleading.

In fact, the separate environment variables page was created for a
reason, which was to have a single place to explain to people unused
to managing their environment how things work, without cluttering
things up for people who already understand this.

There is nothing wrong with small, self-contained guides and in fact I
would argue they are a good thing.

Fix this confusing situation by restoring the original, separate page.

title: canbus: rename zephyr,can-primary chosen property to zephyr,canbus
body:
Rename the Zephyr chosen property for specifying the default CAN bus controller from "zephyr,can-primary" to "zephyr,canbus".

The "zephyr,can-primary" property name was selected in antipation of adding support for redundant CAN networks, which we have yet to add. Meanwhile, the "primary" term causes confusion for non-redundant CAN bus configurations (and the "can" term doesn't match the name of the Zephyr CAN bus subsystem).

The CAN in Automation (CiA) 302-6, which deals with CANopen network redundancy, uses the terms "default interface" and "redundant interface". If/when we add support for redundant CAN networks, the "zephyr,canbus" chosen property can be supplemented with a "zephyr,canbus-redundant" chosen property.

Signed-off-by: Henrik Brix Andersen <hebad@vestas.com>

title: [RFC] doc: replace breathe with Sphinx-Doxygen bridge
body:
This PR adds a new extension that converts Sphinx C domain roles (e.g., ``:c:func:`zephyr_api_call` ``) to links to Doxygen pages.

The end goal is to use Doxygen and not breathe to render APIs. There are a few reasons to do that:

- Doxygen is faster to render API docs (hard to measure “how faster” as not all API are part of Sphinx today).
- As of today, not all APIs are rendered using breathe, creating a sort of incomplete documentation
- Doxygen renders everything automatically, there is no need to explicitly enable groups
- Doxygen docs look & feel is now more in line with Zephyr docs

Sphinx should still be the central place for documentation: GSG, usage guidelines, examples, tutorials, etc. These are the type of docs where rich content is important and where Sphinx is clearly better than Doxygen.

Note: The extension is a proof of concept, so it may have issues (e.g., PDF not supported yet, does not support incremental builds properly, etc.).

Live PoC: https://teslabs.github.io/zephyr-doctest/

title: Adds a k_pipe_flush() API
body:
Fixes #21512

This set of commits adds two pipe flush APIs: k_pipe_buffer_flush() and k_pipe_flush().

k_pipe_buffer_flush() clears out just the specified pipe's ring buffer. If there were threads pending to write into this buffer, then they will attempt write into the buffer just as if another thread had issued a k_pipe_get() call and read those same bytes from the pipe. Thus, it is analogous to reading buffer size bytes into a temporary and then discarding the buffer (but without using a temporary buffer).

k_pipe_flush() builds upon this idea and flushes not just all the data in the pipe's ring buffer, but also all the data waiting to be written to the pipe.

To this end, k_pipe_get(), k_pipe_flush() and k_pipe_buffer_flush() now become wrappers to a common internal interface--pipe_get_internal(). It is expected that when users/developers call k_pipe_get() they specify a valid buffer into which to read the data, which in turn passes that buffer to pipe_get_internal(). The two new flush routines pass NULL instead of a valid buffer to pipe_get_internal(). This allows the bulk of the pipe logic to remain unchanged and minimize the addition of code to support this enhancement.

Along with this, there are a few other minor items cleaned up in the pipe code as this seemed like a good opportunity to do so.
 1. Some build warnings related to void pointer arithmetic have been resolved.
 2. References to asynchronous writes to the pipe have been removed as their support was removed months ago.
 3. k_pipe_cleanup() has been beefed up to fix a race condition.

title: pm: domains: Initial power domain support
body:
Add support for power domains on Zephyr. Power domains are implemented as simple devices so they can use the existent Zephyr API, for resume and suspend sync and async and also reference count.  

- Power domain drivers are responsible for notifying child devices of state changes themselves.
- Custom drivers can be notified and handle transition failures if they wish.
- Power domain transitions are integrated into the existing PM actions, instead of a new set of actions that can occur 
 asynchronously.

The pm subsystem will ensure that domains are resumed before and suspended after devices using them. For device runtime power management, every time the device is got or released the same actions is done to the domain it belongs. 

As domains are implemented as simple devices, it is totally acceptable a domain belongs to another domain.

New changes:

 - Added a  new device action: `PM_DEVICE_ACTION_TURN_ON`
   - `PM_DEVICE_TURN_ON` and `PM_DEVICE_TURN_OFF` actions are used to notifiy devices when the power domain they belong is resuming or suspending.
 - The power domain attribute was moved to `pm.yaml`
 - device runtime is calling `pm_device_state_set` instead of `pm->action_cb` becasuse of the power domain logic that is handled in that function

An overall idea of two devices under a power domain doing runtime power management.

title: pm: device: Simplify device power management
body:
- Remove `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER` and `PM_DEVICE_STATE_OFF` as proposed and discussed in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38619
    - Add new function to query which will be the next power state to be used by the SoC
 -  Change `pm_device_state_set` to align with devices power control callback. Based on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38326
 -  Remove a private header

title: ipc: ipc_service: Rework multi-instance backend.
body:
Only one single IPC service backend is currently present: multi_instance backend. This backend is heavily relying on the RPMsg multi_instance code to instanciate and manage instances and endpoints. Samples exist for both in the samples/subsys/ipc/ directory.

With this patch we are "unpacking" the RPMsg multi_service code to make it more modular and reusable by different backends.

In particular we are re-organizing the code into two helper libraries: an RPMsg library and a VRING / virtqueues static allocation library. At the same time we rewrite the multi_instance backend to make fully use of those new libraries and remove the old multi_instance sample.

This work was suggested as part of the #38328 PR and to be intended as preliminary work to that PR rework.

Please note that this is a rework with no functional changes (indeed no changes required to the IPC service samples).

@arnopo I'm particularly interested in you opinion about the introduction on the RPMsg and static VRINGs helper code and about the naming of those two libraries (or the naming in general I used for the different pieces here).

body:
The goal of this PR is to establish a mechanism which allows to get the offset between system clock on network and application core (assuming they both run from RTC). Add a module which is responsible for getting offset between RTCs
used for system clock on NET and APP cores. After getting an offset

capture feature.

title: pm: device: add action based APIs
body:
This patch adds some new APIs to trigger a device action:

- `pm_device_resume()`
- `pm_device_suspend()`
- `pm_device_turn_off()`
- `pm_device_low_power()`

These APIs are a replacement to the `pm_device_state_set()` API, which
will be removed in subsequent patches. The reason for this removal is
that devices no longer receive a target state but an action to execute,
for example, a device will be told to _suspend_ instead of entering the
_suspended_ state. The current implementation on `pm_device_state_set()`
was selecting the right action to be run based on the given state. This
was done mainly for legacy reasons: `pm_device_state_set` was the only
call available before the transition to actions.

This change allows providing more accurate documentation for each
action, since some of them have subtle requirements that were not clear
enough (e.g. a turned off device can not be suspended).

Note that `pm_device_low_power()` is provided for compatibility, but it
should eventually be replaced by just `pm_device_suspend()`.

title: cmake: APPLICATION_CONFIG_DIR support implemented
body:
With this commit a dedicated APPLICATION_CONFIG_DIR is added to the
Zephyr build system.

Currently, the APPLICATION_SOURCE_DIR is also the base
location of configuration files.

This is very practical for simple samples, but also has its limitations
for more complex setups.

Introducing a dedicated APPLICATION_CONFIG_DIR allows users more
customization options in Zephyr build system.
Especially in terms of custom build configuration files unknown to
Zephyr itself.

For example, instead of all configuration files being located directly
in the application source folder, a project might prefer to organize
their configuration files on a per board basis, for example:
<app>/boards/custom_board_A/prj.conf
<app>/boards/custom_board_A/app.overlay
<app>/boards/custom_board_A/custom_file.mine
<app>/boards/custom_board_B/prj.conf
<app>/boards/custom_board_B/app.overlay
<app>/boards/custom_board_B/custom_file.mine
...

instead of n-files located in the root of the sample.

If the user / sample specifies APPLICATION_CONFIG_DIR, then this folder will
always be used instead of the default configuration folder.

Signed-off-by: Torsten Rasmussen <Torsten.Rasmussen@nordicsemi.no>

title: lvgl: specify ram requirement in sample.yaml
body:
Commit c79b1a38aabe26fc0fbc6bd6af0a5453e8aba95a ("samples: display:
Convert driver and lvgl sample.yaml to use depends_on") started using
depends_on in the sample YAML for a lvgl application instead of
platform_allow.

This breaks build testing with twister and overflow checking enabled
on more resource constrained platforms. The test case's .config
ends up with:

```
    CONFIG_LVGL_HOR_RES_MAX=320
    CONFIG_LVGL_VER_RES_MAX=240
    CONFIG_LVGL_VDB_SIZE=64
    CONFIG_LVGL_BITS_PER_PIXEL=24
```

And lib/gui/lvgl/lvgl.c, where we allocate a buffer of size:

```
    (CONFIG_LVGL_BITS_PER_PIXEL *
     ((CONFIG_LVGL_VDB_SIZE * CONFIG_LVGL_HOR_RES_MAX *
       CONFIG_LVGL_VER_RES_MAX) / 100)
     / 8)
```

Require 147456 bytes to build the sample, ultimately overflowing RAM
if you run something along the lines of:

```
    twister -T samples/.... -p <constrained_platform> --overflow-as-errors
```

This is a reasonable test to be doing to make sure that sample RAM
requirements do not get too big for a subset of platforms that are of
interest, and it no longer works.

To fix it, add a min_ram line for this case so that we can still run
overflow tests on a large set of samples without fine-grained special
casing or creating an ever-growing list of platform excludes for this
test.

I also added a docs patch to make the min_ram (and min_rom) units explicit.

title: Generic Host PCIe Controller Support
body:
This PR is the first step into PCIe Host Controller support on non-x86 platforms (aka Generic or platform-agnostic)

This adds :
- edtlib/gen_defines: changes to handle the ranges DT attribute
- pci-host-ecam-generic bindings
- PCIe Controller API
- Generic PCIe Controller layer implementing the current PCIe API
- Generic PCIe Controller in ECAM mode driver

The Generic PCIe Controller layer provides:
- Configuration space read/write
- single bus endpoint enumerations
- Endpoint I/O, MEM & MEM64 BARs allocation
- Endpoint I/O, MEM & MEM64 BARs get & translation for drivers

The Generic PCIe Controller in ECAM mode driver provides:
- Raw DT RANGES properties into usable PCIe regions
- Configuration space read/write into ECAM config space
- PCIe regions allocation & translation

The limitations are:
- No support for PCIe prefetchable regions
- No support for PCIe bus configuration (only bus0 is supported)
- No support for multiple controllers (no domain-id in BDF)

Support has been designed to initially support Root Complexes with Root Complex Integrated Endpoint, which was designed for Embedded Systems with internal-only PCIe Endpoints on bus 0.

Testing has been done with QEMU with endpoints only on bus0, this can be achieved with:
```
-device <device>,bus=pcie.0
```

MSI/MSI-X support depends on #37506 completion

DT RANGES tooling and macros are pushed to #38106 and this serie is rebased on it, will need to be merged before this one.

Extended PCI(e) capability offset & defines changes were moved to #38256

body: The commit which introduces new pin control helper macros to devicetree.h is: ``` devicetree: add devicetree/pinctrl.h This contains accessor macros for getting phandles out of pinctrl properties by name and index. As usual, the representation in C for a phandle is a node identifier. Add these new macros: - DT_PINCTRL_BY_IDX(node_id, pc_idx, idx): phandle at index idx in the pinctrl- property - DT_PINCTRL_0(node_id, idx): pinctrl-0 convenience for the same - DT_PINCTRL_BY_NAME(node_id, name, idx): phandle at index idx in the pinctrl property named 'name' - DT_PINCTRL_NAME_TO_IDX(node_id, name): convert a pinctrl property name to its index number - DT_NUM_PINCTRLS_BY_IDX(node_id, pc_idx): number of phandles in pinctrl- - DT_NUM_PINCTRLS_BY_NAME(node_id, name): number of phandles in a named pinctrl property - DT_NUM_PINCTRL_STATES(node_id): total number of pinctrl- properties - DT_PINCTRL_HAS_IDX(node_id, pc_idx): does pinctrl- exist? - DT_PINCTRL_HAS_NAME(node_id, name): does a named pinctrl property exist? - DT_PINCTRL_IDX_TO_NAME_TOKEN(node_id, pc_idx): convert a pinctrl index to its name as a token, similar to DT_STRING_TOKEN() - DT_PINCTRL_IDX_TO_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id, pc_idx): like DT_PINCTRL_IDX_TO_NAME_TOKEN, but with an uppercase result As well as DT_DRV_INST equivalents, which take inst wherever node_id appears above: - DT_INST_PINCTRL_BY_IDX() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_0() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_BY_NAME() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_NAME_TO_IDX() - DT_INST_NUM_PINCTRLS_BY_IDX() - DT_INST_NUM_PINCTRLS_BY_NAME() - DT_INST_NUM_PINCTRL_STATES() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_HAS_IDX() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_HAS_NAME() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_IDX_TO_NAME_TOKEN() - DT_INST_PINCTRL_IDX_TO_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN() Signed-off-by: Martí Bolívar ``` The rest of the PR is prep work, bookkeeping, and documentation. --- This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/37644)

title: Sample: Add Bluetooth L2CAP Mesh sample
body:
Hello everyone,
I have been working on several simultaneous Bluetooth Low Energy connections.
However, I encountered problems, mostly assertion errors, while doing a lot of parallel connections.

One example with 20 devices resulted in the following assertion fail:
```
d_14: @00:00:21.215881  ASSERTION FAIL [err == 0] @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c:305
d_14: @00:00:21.215881  	k_sem_take failed with err -11
d_14: @00:00:21.215881  @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c:305
d_14: @00:00:21.215881 WARNING: Exiting due to fatal error
```

I think that race conditions due to many connections result in undesired behavior of the BLE stack. Therefore, I built this specific, simplified example that bases on parallel connections: Devices create a sort of connection-oriented BLE mesh. They advertise and directly connect to other devices, sending dummy data over L2CAP channels.
I believe an example like this may aid in solving or even uncovering issues such as https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/30245 , https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/36381, or https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/25917  .
The multi-device environment is simulated using BabbleSim and should be easily tweaked for testing purposes as well.

What would you think of such a sample (or a respective test case)?

title: Redefine iterable section APIs for external use
body:
Hi,

Zephyr has a small set of macros for handling iterable sections. These are used in various places for finding lists of statically initialized things such as thread, mutexes etc...

The same functionality can be really useful for external applications as well (they are actually already used in the Nordic SDK). This PR redefines aliases of the APIs to drop the Z_ qualifier, which identifies them as internal, and exposes the associated documentation in a new page under the "API References" section, making theme more suitable for use outside of the core code base.

One open question: should we standardize all the macros to use the `ITERABLE_SECTION_` prefix? (such as `ITERABLE_SECTION`, `ITERABLE_SECTION_ALTERNATE` and `ITERABLE_SECTION_FOREACH`)

title: ztest: Add register functionality
body:
Add new functionality to ztest to improve test modularity. The two
primary new entry points are:
* ztest_register_test_suite
* ztest_run_registered_test_suites

When registering a new test suite, users provide the name as well as
an optional pragma used to filter the tests for each run. Using NULL
as the pragma ensures that the test is run exactly once (after which
it is removed from the linked list of test suites).

Calls to ztest_run_registered_test_suites take a state pointer as an
argument. This allows the the pragma functions to decide whether the
test should be run (see the BT and accel tests as an example of using
the global test state as a filter).

The biggest benefit of this system (other than the ability to filter
tests and maintain a larger test state) is the ability to better
modularize the test source code. In the example of basicmath, main.c
doesn't need to (or should) know about q7, q15, q31, or f32's test
suites. Instead, each source file manages registering its own test
suite and handling the conditions for running the suite.

Signed-off-by: Yuval Peress <peress@chromium.org>

title: random: deprecate xoroshiro128+ in favor of xoshiro128++
body:
Deprecate the xoroshiro128+ PRNG algorithm in favour of xoshiro128++. xoshiro128++ is a drop-in replacement which is invisible from the user perspective.

xoroshiro128+ is unsuitable because it is explicitly a floating-point PRNG, not a general-purpose PRNG. This means that the lower 4 bits of the output are actually linear, not random (from the designers, https://prng.di.unimi.it/). This means 1/8th of the generated data is not random.

Additionally, xoroshiro128+ is not a 32bit algorithm, it operates on 64bit numbers. For the vast majority of Zephyr devices, this makes the PRNG slower than it needs to be. The replacement (xoshiro128++) is 32bit, with no loss in state space (still 128 bit).

title: net: lwm2m: Fix floating point handling
body:
I've identified several issues when I tried to fix a problem with floating-point resource writes (see commit messages for details).

In general, I've:
1. Dumped the differentiation between 32/64 bit float values in LwM2M engine, and focused on `float32_value`, which was most commonly used. The actual handling between 32/64 bit floats takes only place when TLVs are being parsed (and the actual type is identified based on the TLV size, as described in the specification).
2. Fixed the Plain Text formatter, which incorrectly parsed floating points.
3. Fixed JSON formatter, which had the same issue as above.
4. Fixed a few other issues in JSON formatter, which prevented successful writes in general.

I was actually considering to dump both float types defined by LwM2M and replace them with native `float` or `double`. Replacing `float32_value_t` with `double` should have minimal (if any) memory footprint impact and would increase the precision of the LwM2M floating point handling a lot. As it is a more invasive change to the engine however, I wanted to hear some opinions first, but for me, the use of `float32_value_t` is a bit counter-intuitive (and more difficult from the application point of view).

body:
The main purpose of this pull request is to audit the nRF SoC .dtsi files and ensure they all have any missing RADIO, FICR, UICR, and EGU nodes.

Adding the missing RADIO nodes in particular is a prerequisite for implementing #30708, which will add a `fem` property to the radio nodes that will allow for configuring the PA/LNA hardware. The rest are just cleanups while I'm here.

While doing this, I noticed that I couldn't really add RADIO nodes for SoCs that don't support the Bluetooth Direction Finding Extension (DFE). This is because all the DFE related properties in the RADIO nodes are marked `required`, which in my opinion doesn't make much sense to add to e.g. the nRF52840 .dtsi file, since that SoC doesn't support DFE.

Therefore, as prep work for the prep work, this PR also reorganizes the DFE support by making all the related properties optional, and adds a new `dfe-supported` property that can be used to test if a given RADIO peripheral supports the extension. That requires some changes to the related controller implementation and bindings documentation, so I took the opportunity to try to do some other docs improvements as well.
