title: Clarify device power states
body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

As of today, there is no clear guidance on what device power states really mean on Zephyr. As a result of this problem, most (if not all) devices treat all "low power states" as a single state. In the end, this results in device drivers that do not behave according to any specification and so may result in unexpected behavior.

Let's start analyzing the current defined states:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/559135721732eac1180885def818cc1d3d65d0b9/include/pm/device.h#L27-L52

- `PM_DEVICE_STATE_ACTIVE`: This state is quite clear, the device is _turned on_ and operational.
- `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER`: Here we start having problems. What is the difference between `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER` and `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND`? Other than context preservation, there is no clear difference. Should a device implement suspend or low power actions? Or both? Before moving to action based PM hooks, most drivers did the following, _just in case_:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/5b5396f7b6ff84f12553d9e16207df0cce7e19e7/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c#L285-L296

This pattern is now gone from all in-tree drivers, and no drivers required to implement any _low power_ action during the transition to action based callback. The example above has now become:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/c3050a5aab1e86d02642eb4c6a027419e6a3a096/drivers/i2c/i2c_nrfx_twim.c#L256-L281

The only remaining user of the low power state is the system PM, which uses low power vs. suspend depending on the system transition:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/c2897c6b18121fa7733cbb9ad7e0207e4ba2054b/subsys/pm/power.c#L210-L235

However, no in-tree drivers support such state and it is inconsistent with the runtime PM framework, where only the suspend state is used.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

If we look at the ACPI specification, we have the following states:

| State  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| D0     | This state is assumed to be the highest level of power consumption. The device is completely active and responsive, and is expected to remember all relevant context continuously.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| D1     | The meaning of the D1 Device State is defined by each device class. Many device classes may not define D1. In general, D1 is expected to save less power and preserve more device context than D2.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| D2     | The meaning of the D2 Device State is defined by each device class. Many device classes may not define D2. In general, D2 is expected to save more power and preserve less device context than D1 or D0. Buses in D2 may cause the device to lose some context (for example, by reducing power on the bus, thus forcing the device to turn off some of its functions).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D3hot  | The meaning of the D3hot State is defined by each device class. In general, D3hot is expected to save as much power as possible without affecting PNP Enumeration. Devices in D3hot must have enough power to remain enumerable by software. For example, PCI Configuration space access and contents must operate as in shallower power states. Similarly, ACPI identification and configuration objects must operate as in shallower power states. Otherwise, no device functionality is supported, and Driver software is required to restore any lost context, or reinitialize the device, during its transition back to D0. Devices in this state can have long restore times. All classes of devices define this state. |
| D3cold | Power has been fully removed from the device. Also referred to as D3cold in this and other specs. All device context is lost when this state is entered, so the OS software will reinitialize the device when powering it back on. Since all device context and power are lost, devices in this state do not decode their address lines, and cannot be enumerated by software. Devices in this state have the longest restore times.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Ref. https://uefi.org/sites/default/files/resources/ACPI_6_3_final_Jan30.pdf (2.3)

It looks like Windows is using this model for device power management, see: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/device-power-states. They even define the allowed state transitions, which is something interesting to have predictable behavior:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/126304209-3e46529b-8bd5-400f-86e4-21e12bcf2ccd.png)

ACPI seems to be a little less restrictive on allowed transitions:

> Transitions amongst these power states are restricted for simplicity. Power-down transitions (from
higher-power, or shallower, to lower-power, or deeper) are allowed between any two states. However,
power-up transitions (from deeper to shallower) are required to go through D0; i.e. Dy to Dx<y is illegal
for all x !=0.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/126303600-58f797bd-1043-405c-92f3-eed3edc6a1e6.png)

The following table provides a tentative mapping between ACPI and Zephyr states:

| ACPI State | Zephyr state                                             |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| D0         | `PM_DEVICE_STATE_ACTIVE`                                 |
| D1         | ?                                                        |
| D2         | ?                                                        |
| D3hot      | `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND` or `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER` |
| D3cold     | `PM_DEVICE_STATE_OFF`                                    |

Some initial observations:

- `D1` and `D2` have no clear mapping to Zephyr states
- `D3hot` may have two possible candidates, even though `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND` seems the best candidates since it's the only low power state used by the runtime PM framework.

The proposed solution/s:

- ~~Remove `PM_DEVICE_STATE_FORCE_SUSPEND` since it does not represent an actual state.~~
- Clarify the difference between `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND` and `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER`. Possibly stay with just `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND` and delete `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER` since the runtime framework does not use it.
- ~~Decide if transitional states can be replaced with a sort of "transitioning" flag for all transitions.~~
- Decide if, for now, it is worth adding support for D1 and D2 type of states. If multiple low power states are supported, this likely means a sort of device PM policy will be required to decide which low power (D1, D2, D3x) state has to be used.
- Update documentation:
  - Clarify states meaning
  - Add details on ACPI mapping
  - Provide some device implementation guidance
  - Document allowed transitions 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

N/A

N/A

title: Improve (k_)malloc and heap documentation
body:
In Zephyr there are two kinds of heaps:

- kernel-provided heaps
- libc-provided heap

Kernel-provided heaps (among them system heap) are documented here: https://developer.nordicsemi.com/nRF_Connect_SDK/doc/latest/zephyr/reference/kernel/memory/heap.html#heap-v2

As for libc-provided heaps, matters are more complicated. First of all there are several types of C library (among them minimal libc and newlib). These libraries have their own heap that provides memory for malloc() (the kernel-provided system heap provides memory for k_malloc()).

How this libc-provided heap is configured depends on many variables: MPU, userspace, MMU etc.

What would be necessary is to have a `(k_)malloc` guide or section, that describes where and how memory is allocated depending on which options and APIs are used.

title: pm: device power management improvements
body:
Summary:

- Remove usage of local states, the device PM subsystem already holds device PM state
- The "ctrl_command" is removed, since the PM control callback will now always be called to set the state, not to retrieve it.
- The state is passed as a value, since it does not need to be written by the PM control callback
- The callback is only called for a state change, thus simplifying driver operation (no need for state change checks)
- Converged _low power_ states to `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND`. This makes interoperability between system and device PM easier. The low power state is still kept, but its future is unclear and needs some discussion.
- Device PM control function return codes are now documented.
- Multiple implementation cleanups.
- Introduction of the _actions_ concept. Devices will now receive actions instead of states, for example, a device will be told to "suspend" or to "resume".

title: Add support for FPGA controllers
body:
This PR adds a new FPGA subsystem which allows users to control FPGA chips using Zephyr.

The main part is the FPGA controller itself. It is a completely new Zephyr subsystem developed to enable communication between Zephyr and FPGAs.

The FPGA controller has been created to:
* have control over the FPGA from Zephyr
* enable bitstream loading into the FPGA

The work on the controller consisted of several parts:
* a completely new API, which enables the users to check the status of the FPGA chip, power it on or off, and change the contents of the reprogrammable logic
* FPGA drivers, the controller currently supports the EOS S3 chip with its embedded FPGA (we are also working on support for Zynq US+ - it is not yet ready but we have a working prototype)
* a new Zephyr shell command which allows users to check the status, control and reprogram the FPGA using the Zephyr shell subsystem

In addition to that, a `devmem load` command has been created. It can be seen here: #36010. It allows users to load arbitrary data to the memory of a board running Zephyr over the serial interface. It ties well with the FPGA subsystem, it can be used to easily transfer bitstream files into the memory, and later load them onto the FPGA using the new controller subsystem.

Examples of use along with sample output can be seen [here](https://github.com/antmicro/zephyr-fpga-controller-examples) (note that this might not include all the latest changes in the PRs that we've made after the reviews but shows the concept as a whole).

title: task_wdt: Fix the way the kernel timer is used
body:
Do not use periodic executions of the timer handler, as in certain
circumstances (the fallback hardware watchdog used, one or more
task_wdt channel activated but none of them being ever fed) this
would lead to no callback/reset being executed for any channel.
Instead, schedule the next timeout from the timer handler function
when the function is executed for the dummy background channel or
for a channel that was deleted.

This fixes #36357.

Use the actual minimum timeout used by the sample for task watchdog
channels (100 ms) as the configuration value for the fallback hardware
watchdog, to avoid unnecessary executions of the timer handler.

Add missing indentation in the documentation of the sample so that
the console output is rendered correctly.

title: Use a custom role for Kconfig configuration options
body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
We are misusing :option: to mark and reference Kconfig options. This role is for command line options and not for configuration options. If you look at https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/genindex-C.html you will see that it is being indexed as command line options in a very user unfriendly way.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If there is no role that would give us what we need, create a custom role :config: and use that instead.

We can also skip the indexing, because the configuration options index is created by us anyways, no need to have any of those options listed in the main index generated by sphinx.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Use pre-existing role, but I could not find anything suitable.

title: drivers: display: reimplementation of micro:bit display
body:
Reimplementation of LED matrix driver for micro:bit. Here is why:

- It is compatible both with micro:bit V1 and V2
- It improves the rendering by rendering pixels rather than lines (the latter causes uneven luminosity), while maintaining a low system load.

This is achieved by using a hardware timer of the SOC for pixel refresh interrupts and by an optimized pixel refresh ISR. The estimated maximum load while the screen is active is less than 1%, maybe 0.5%. The timing of pixel refreshing and animation is separated. We use delayable kwork for the animation.

The driver is rewritten from sketch. I have tested it with both micro:bit V1 and V2. It's behaviour should be very similar to the original driver on V1.

So far, the only sample I have adapted is samples/boards/bbc_microbit/display. The only change needed was to require an NRFX_TIMER to be enabled. I will go through the other demos on V1, the trouble is, some of them still won't work on V2 for other reasons.

Happy to receive your comments.

title: devicetree.h is stable
body:
This API meets the requirements for marking an API stable:

- Test cases for the new API with 100% coverage: yes;
  we have had coverage for every API macro since the beginning.

- Complete documentation in code. All public interfaces shall be
  documented and available in online documentation.: yes, in the
  reference documentation:
  https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/devicetree/api.html

- The API has been in-use and was available in at least 2 development
  releases: yes; this API was introduced in v2.3.

The basic design involving node identifiers and the macros that create
and operate on them has not changed since the API was introduced, and
it is in widespread use throughout the tree. As we head into a new
LTS, it's time to mark it stable.

This is more of an acknowledgement of reality than a big change, as I
don't see any backwards incompatible changes since the API was first
introduced in v2.3. (We have deprecated a lot of label related macros
that are no longer required now that we have DEVICE_DT_GET and
friends, but they're still there, and we're still testing them, just
as if this were a stable API.)

title: [RFC] pm: device power management improvements
body:
This RFC PR is an initial attempt to simplify the current device PM callback and fix some other issues. Even though the change set is large (all drivers have been ported), the behavior _should_ be the same as before. Only a few existing issues have been fixed, but there are many that still need to be addressed. As a result of these changes, adding support for device PM should be less cumbersome.

The list of changes can be summarized to:
1. Local power states are removed, device PM holds the device state
2. The "ctrl_command" is gone (`uint32_t ctrl_command`), devices are now called with the action they should perform: `static int my_device_pm_control(const struct device *dev, enum pm_device_action action)`.
3. Device PM control function is only called if needed. This means that devices are only called if the requested action will change the current state (e.g. a suspended device will not be called with `PM_DEVICE_ACTION_SUSPEND`).
4. `PM_DEVICE_STATE_FORCE_SUSPEND` has been removed since it did not represent any actual state and was not used.
5. `PM_DEVICE_STATE_LOW_POWER` has been replaced for `PM_DEVICE_STATE_SUSPEND`, since they were equivalents.
6. Device PM control function return codes are now documented.
7. Multiple implementation cleanups

**NOTE: This PR should only be taken as a reference, smaller changes will be submitted as new PRs.**

title: Mere warnings slow down incremental documentation build from seconds to minutes
body:
**Describe the bug**

Making a typo and trying to build the documentation make it last minutes instead of seconds. Even a simple warning seems to break the incremental build.

I don't remember this performance issue happening in the past. Regression caused by #33934 maybe?


**To Reproduce**
```
$ cd zephyr
$ time make -C doc # a few minutes as expected
$ time make -C doc # a couple seconds as expected: incremental build.
```
```
$ printf '\n\nsome text\n' >> doc/guides/west/build-flash-debug.rst
$ time make -C doc # incremental build takes seconds, nice
```
Now insert a warning in /doc/guides/west/build-flash-debug.rst (or some other file)
```
$ printf '`missing quote\n' >> doc/guides/west/build-flash-debug.rst
$ time make -C doc # fails instantly the first time, nice
$ time make -C doc # takes a few minutes again, not nice
```
Fixing the typo immediately after the first failure does not help: it does not make the second build fast.


**Expected behavior**

Making a typo when writing documentation should not cost minutes.

**Impact**

Serious loss of time and strong incentive to cut documentation corners.

title: Add support for Everlight B1414 LED strip controller
body:
This PR allows to use the ws2812_spi led-strip driver with the Everlight B1414 LED controller.

The B1414 controller shares a lot of characteristics with the WS2812. But there are few differences:

- The latch / reset delay is 250 microseconds (against 8 for the WS2812).
- The color or pixel order depends on the model (while it seems to be fixed to GBR for the WS2812).
- Each bit of the control signal (waveform) is described with a 1.2 us pulse:
   0 bit: 300 ns high and 900 ns low.
   1 bit: 900 ns high and 300 ns low.
   With a +/- 80 ns tolerance for each timing.

In order to address this differences, this PR:

- Adds the "color-mapping" and "reset-delay" property to the WS2812 DT binding.
- Updates the ws2812_gpio and ws2812_spi drivers accordingly.
- Replaces k_busy_wait() with k_usleep() in the ws2812_spi driver.
- Adds some information about the B1414 LED controller to the WS2812 DT binding.
- And finally provides an usage example through the led_ws2812 sample.

title: ARM: cortex-M: qemu: add support for executing tests with FPU/FPU_SHARING
body:
We are adding support for running tests and samples in CI for QEMU on Cortex-M with FPU and FPU_SHARING options enabled. **This fixes a severe limitation we had until now, by not covering at all the ARCH/Kernel implementation around Floating Point support in QEMU, at least not for Cortex-M. This is important for Zephyr LTS release.**

The solution is a bit complex, and involves extending the remote-core (CPU1) target of MPS2 AN521, since FPU support is only emulated on CPU1. The patch re-organizes a bit the AN521 SoC and board(s) definitions accordingly.

Effectively, we add support (locally for AN521) for multi-image builds, because the CPU1 binaries cannot run as standalone images. While it is desired to have a generic multi-image solution, we currently restricted the implementation to the AN521 board, to address our (important) use-case, without making drastic changes to Zephyr build framework.

title: cmake: tfm: support for custom CMake args when building TF-M
body:
This commit allows a subsystem to specify additional CMake flags to be
given to the TF-M build.

The additional CMake flags can be provided through the TFM_CMAKE_OPTIONS
property on the zephyr_property_target.
Using the zephyr_property_target allows Zephyr modules to append extra
TFM_CMAKE_OPTIONS regardless of the CMake processing order.

It splits the ExternalProject_Add into a two step process with the CMake
invocation executed using add_custom_target() and the build process
using ExternalProject_Add(). The reason for this split is because CMake
generator expressions passed through ExternalProject_Add to CMake will
quoted so that `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:<tgt>,<prop>>` becomes
`"-DFOO=bar -DBAR=foo"` instead of `-DFOO=bar -DBAR=foo` which again
results in CMake failures.

title: arm64: FPU context switching support
body:
This adds support for FPU context switching (FPU sharing) to the ARM64
architecture.

The compiler may insert FPU reg accesses in anycontext to optimize even
non-FP code unless the `-mgeneral-regs-only` compiler flag is used,
but Zephyr currently doesn't support such a build, and linked libraries
might not have used that flag either, etc.

Related: #32192, #32195, #33229

This basically means that Zephyr on ARM64 is somewhat risky as any
thread may clobber the FP register of any other threads. We got away
with it so far because most of the time, FP usage happens rarely, or
is used within memset() with the value 0, or in other words by luck.

This PR adds the necessary FPU sharing code so that at least full FPU
usage is properly supported.

This is based on top of PRs #34118 and #34323 which are therefore included
here as well.

title: [RFC] TensorFlow Lite Micro as a module
body:
## Issue
#34295 

## Introduction
Adds the TensorFlow Lite Micro library as a Zephyr module and incorporates two TensorFlow Lite Micro samples into the tree for reference.

## Problem description
Unless they're willing to do legwork similar to this PR on their own, developers of TensorFlow apps on Zephyr build inside the TensorFlow tree with a Makefile generated from a template that invokes CMake and Make. Developers are not able to interact directly with `CMakeLists.txt`, `prj.conf` and other build settings / options in the ways to which they may be accustomed.

## Proposed change

Allow users to build TensorFlow apps on Zephyr in the usual way (i.e. with west).

- Add TensorFlow as a Zephyr module with a Kconfig option
- Incorporate two TensorFlow Lite Micro samples for reference

## Detailed RFC

### Proposed change (detailed)

- Add TensorFlow 2.4.1 with static copies of third-party library dependencies
  - (See [the RFC-version of the TensorFlow Zephyr module repository](https://github.com/laurenmurphyx64/tensorflow). This is temporary and will be updated with a reference to the official Zephyr Project's TensorFlow repository.)
  -  Avoid replicating bash scripts to pull and patch these copies
  - (See `Dependencies` and `Concerns and Unresolved Questions` for further discussion)
- Add a single Kconfig option for enabling TensorFlow (for now) (`CONFIG_TENSORFLOW`)
- Add TensorFlow Hello World sample for most boards (build and run test case for QEMU in CI)
- Add TensorFlow Magic Wand sample for LiteX/VexRiscV emulated by Renode (build-only test case in CI)

### Dependencies
- [TensorFlow](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow) [2.4.1](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/releases/tag/v2.4.1) ([Apache 2.0 License](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/LICENSE))
- [Antmicro's LiteX/VexRiscv demo with emulation on Renode](https://github.com/antmicro/litex-vexriscv-tensorflow-lite-demo/) ([Apache-2.0 License](https://github.com/antmicro/litex-vexriscv-tensorflow-lite-demo/blob/master/LICENSE)) 
  - See also [their blog post](https://antmicro.com/blog/2019/12/tflite-in-zephyr-on-litex-vexriscv/), which was also [cross-posted onto the Zephyr blog in 2019](https://www.zephyrproject.org/tensorflow-lite-in-zephyr-rtos-on-litex-vexriscv/) with an [update in 2020](https://www.zephyrproject.org/running-and-testing-tensorflow-lite-on-microcontrollers-without-hardware-in-renode/)
- [FlatBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers) by Google ([Apache 2.0 License](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/blob/master/LICENSE.txt))
- [Gemmlowp](https://github.com/google/gemmlowp) by Google ([Apache 2.0 License](https://github.com/google/gemmlowp/blob/master/LICENSE))
- [Ruy](https://github.com/google/ruy) by Google ([Apache 2.0 License](https://github.com/google/ruy/blob/master/LICENSE))

#### Note

In the TensorFlow build system, the last three are pulled in as specific versions from mirror repositories with only certain files and patched by TensorFlow's bash scripts. I copied these patched files into a `third_party_static/` static directory in [my RFC version](https://github.com/laurenmurphyx64/tensorflow/) of the TensorFlow Zephyr module repository. See [the commit history of that repository](https://github.com/laurenmurphyx64/tensorflow/commits/zephyr) for more information about these dependencies.

## Notes, Concerns and Unresolved Questions

### Future porting of the Magic Wand sample to an actual board
I've been working on porting the Magic Wand sample to `frdm_k64f` for use with the FXOS8700 accelerometer, but hit a roadblock. The port will be added in a future PR.

### Building for LiteX VexRiscV in CI
If the GitHub CI doesn't already build for `litex_vexriscv`, we would need to add that so the Magic Wand sample is built along with the other samples.

### Static Third-Party Libraries

As mentioned before, TensorFlow uses several bash scripts to generate a Makefile from a template and download and patch certain files of specific versions of three third-party dependencies. Instead of attempting to duplicate that, I put a static copy of these files into my RFC version of the TensorFlow repository. We might want to think about whether it's a good idea (and if it's possible) to replicate those scripts and invoke them in the Zephyr build process. 

Regardless of what we decide to do, the owner of the TensorFlow Zephyr module will need to monitor the upstream to make sure we get any updates on the dependencies. The versions as well as the patches applied by the bash scripts might change in future releases of TensorFlow.

- [FlatBuffers commit](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/commit/dca12522a9f9e37f126ab925fd385c807ab4f84e) dated September 24, 2020
- [Gemmlowp commit](https://github.com/google/gemmlowp/commit/719139ce755a0f31cbf1c37f7f98adcc7fc9f425) dated September 4, 2018
- [Ruy commit](https://github.com/google/ruy/commit/4790797d11a81f96baf24f3731fd3ca44c2c5f8b) dated November 15, 2020
- [TensorFlow download_and_extract.sh](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/make/download_and_extract.sh) last updated January 5th

title: Add Cortex-R82 Support
body:
This PR introduces the [Cortex-R82](https://developer.arm.com/ip-products/processors/cortex-r/cortex-r82) processor for Zephyr, which is a 64-bit Real-time Processor.
Cortex-R82 is the highest performance real-time processor from Arm and the first to implement the Armv8-R AArch64 architecture.

Since the Cortex-R82 is new, only Arm FVP (Arm [Fixed Virtual Platforms](https://developer.arm.com/tools-and-software/simulation-models/fixed-virtual-platforms)) can simulate the Cortex-R82. To boot Zephyr with Cortex-R82, we also introduce a new SoC named `fvp_aemv8r` and a new board named `fvp_baser_aemv8r`.
Similar to Cortex-A, Cortex-R82 supports arm generic timer and GICv3.

The GCC 10 doesn't support `-mcpu=cortex-r82`, so we use `-march=armv8.4-a` as a workaround. We will fix it once the new GCC supports Cortex-R82.
Currently, the FVP of Cortex-R82 hasn't been released officially, so the fvp_baser_aemv8r board is only available for build.
But the good news is the FVP release date is soon, and we have already enabled the ztest with the FVP. Except for the samples/arch/mpu/mpu_test (designed for aarch32), we have passed all the 281 test cases, and here is the report.

title: Changes to bluetooth mesh for k_work API
body:
This PR supports #33104 in updating the use of k_work delayable timers in the Bluetooth mesh implementation.  The API has been updated, and appears to work on one sample with limited testing.

It is in draft format, and all commits tagged DNM, because this needs significant review and rework from domain experts to address the following concerns.  More details are in comments in the code, and in the individual commit messages.  At least one unrelated probable bug has been highlighted (in cfg_srv).  Overall:

On the whole this code does not appear to be correct in the presence of preemptive threads or SMP systems.  The use of atomic flags without an enclosing lock for operations that are not read-modify-write is not robust in those contexts.

There were many uses of `k_delayed_work_cancel()`, none of which took into account the possibility that cancellation can fail, and several of which would likely cause faults if the work item continued to be after the post-cancellation state updates were made.

It is generally not clear whether schedule or reschedule operations are appropriate.

My preferred path forward is for a mesh maintainer to take these commits and rework them as necessary.

(NB: This is currently based on and incorporates #33614 to support the sample.)

title: Modularisation and Restructuring of Documentation
body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Zephyr documentation currently is composed of different sources  all tied together through one single and long build process that collects data from the different sources, coverts the information into the final format and links everything into what we get on docs.zephyrproject.org. 

The whole process is very long and on some machines can take up to 15-20 minutes, basically building everything we have, including:
- doxygen documentation converted from XML to RST using breathe
- Kconfig reference from Kconfig files converted into RST using custom scripts
- Devicetree bindings reference from binding files converted into RST using custom scripts
- board documentation in RST collected from the source tree using custom extensions
- sample/test documentation in RST collected from the source tree using custom extensions
- and finally the documentation under doc/ which is structured in a way to allow integrating the above sources

Right now it is either you build the whole thing or nothing. Some steps were taken to reduce the time by skipping the generation of lengthy reference pages (Kconfig), but things are still very slow.

Another limitation is related to the fact that we are not able to publish or build a subset of the documentation for different use cases. For example, to build a printable reference of Zephyr in PDF we would have to include everything that we have on the online version and there is no way to control how things are structured and what information end up in such a reference. If you are using the Zephyr documentation to support a product, you might be interested in including only the sections of the documentation relevant to your product, supported subsystems and hardware and not documentation of all samples and boards that come with Zephyr.

For Zephyr itself, there is a desire to produce documentation for only a subset of the features and be selective about what ends up in the final document, this requires a well structured documentation layout in general and a well defined and controlled content to allow for extraction of information without breaking cross-references and linkage. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- At the first level, we need to think about how to restructure the documentation in the most optimal way to support the above, basically 
  - adapt and optimize the tree structure, 
  - group sections if applicable, 
  - establish a standard for how sections are added and where they are added, and
  - standardize index pages and how we show table of content in sub-sections
- Provide a mechanism to allow customization of the docs based on the output and intended use. There is a difference between a catch-all online reference and a programming and developer reference. For example we could establish a set of "chapters" in an imaginary book:
   - Introduction, What is Zephyr, etc.
   - Getting Started: Environment setup, etc.
   - Developer Guide: Development with Zephyr, Debugging, etc.
   - Architecture of Zephyr, Device Model, Architecture support, Configuration system, etc.
   - Subsystem and Core OS documentation
   - API Reference
   - Board Reference
   - Sample Reference
   - Configuration option reference
   - etc.
 
Through configuration options it should then be possible to select any of the above to create the desired output, but it should also be possible to filter content of each chapter if it makes sense, for example, limit the board reference to a certain vendor, or filter out samples that are not relevant to the mode of output.

The above could be done in one single documentation instance, but could also be done in multiple instance that are linked together using the current doc build system. This would also improve the build speed and eventually would allow building documentation parallel (?)

title: kernel: rework kobject metadata generation not to use gperf
body:
Due to the use of gperf to generate hash table for kobjects, the addresses of these kobjects cannot change during the last few phases of linking (especially between zephyr_prebuilt.elf and zephyr.elf). Because of this, the gperf generated data needs to be placed at the end of memory to avoid pushing symbols around in memory. This prevents moving these generated blocks to earlier sections, for example, pinned data section needed for demand paging.
    
This changes how the kobject list is generated. Instead of using gperf, our own script now generates C source file containing the list. Since the number of kobjects is consistent (once started building), the size of this list remains constant throughout different stages of linking, and thus no longer requires putting all related data structures at the end of RAM. Note that non-final version of the list still is needed to be linked in intermediate binaries so the addresses of the kobjects would remain constant at later linker stages.

Alternative to #33687

title: Tracing: Trace system overhaul
body:
Adds generic trace hook macros for inserting trace hook for
function entry, exit, blocking, and object initialization
with a variable number of arguments (objects, return values,
etc.). Utilizing macro concatenation these macros produce
trace hooks of a similar format to the old trace system
with `SYS_TRACING_OBJ_FUNC(k_thread, switched_in)` being
turned into `sys_trace_k_thread_switched_in()` by the
preprocessor. Although these macros still rely on the manual
definition of each unique trace hook in tracing.h, the benefit
of not directly calling those is that we can enable/disable
trace hooks based on object type (`k_thread`, `k_sem`, etc.)
through the preprocessor while providing the ability of adding
type specific runtime trace processing similar to
`SYS_TRACING_OBJ_INIT`.

Adds tracing hooks to most kernel objects to enable tracing of
core behavior/state and functionality that affects application
scheduling. This improves on the previous tracing hooks which
only covered a fraction of the important events within Zephyr.

Adds syscall tracing by injecting syscall entry/exit tracing
hooks as `__syscall` functions are parsed by the `gen_syscalls.py`
script.

Note 1: Since this tracing system overhaul currently co-exists
with the previous system, all new trace hooks and macros use a
`sys_port_trace` or `SYS_PORT_TRACING` notation to avoid conflicts.
This notation with an extra port/PORT infix should be removed
if this system is adopted over the previous system.

Note 2: To enable tracing of return values many new trace hooks
required the decomposition of return statements. Although these
changes should be safe it is important that the respective code
owners verify that there are no unintended side-effects.

Note 3: Tracing of calls like `k_msleep` can cause problems
with User Mode threads since these will potentially invoke
trace code that is outside their domain. If possible these
should be migrated to have their own `__syscall` wrapper similar
to `k_sleep`.

Note 4: Several static inline functions defined in kernel.h
were changed into declarations with definitions in their
respective kernel object source file. This was done to
facilitate tracing and avoid including the entire tracing
system in `kernel.h`.

title: doc: application: Document using west outside of workspace
body:
This PR adds a note to the "Application Development" page, explaining that using west outside of a west workspace needs `ZEPHYR_BASE` to be set.

The current instructions on the "Application Development" use `west` outside of a west workspace, but do not tell you to set your `ZEPHYR_BASE` variable. This causes an error when running `west` commands which is difficult to understand.

----

Currently, if you follow the instructions on the "Application Development" page without having `ZEPHYR_BASE` set, you will get the error:

```west: error: argument <command>: invalid choice: 'build' (choose from 'init', 'update', 'list', 'manifest', 'diff', 'status', 'forall', 'help', 'config', 'topdir', 'selfupdate')```

The "Troubleshooting West" has a section for this error, explaining you need to [set the ZEPHYR_BASE environment variable](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/guides/west/troubleshooting.html#invalid-choice-build-or-flash-etc) to build outside of a `.west` workspace.

In Zephyr 2.2.0 and below, the ["Getting Started Guide"](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/2.2.0/getting_started/index.html#build-the-blinky-application) and ["Application Development"](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/2.2.0/application/index.html#important-build-system-variables) pages told you
to run `zephyr-env.sh/zephyr-env.cmd` which would set `ZEPHYR_BASE`, but this documentation was removed
in Zephyr 2.3.0. The Zephyr 2.3.0 changelog states ["registering the Zephyr CMake package in the CMake user package registry removes the need for setting of ZEPHYR_BASE, sourcing zephyr-env.sh, or running zephyr-env.cmd"](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/releases/release-notes-2.3.html#build-and-infrastructure). I'm guessing it was overlooked that `ZEPHYR_BASE` is still required for out-of-workspace usage of `west`.

As a side note, there are still some references to `zephyr-env.sh/zephyr-env.cmd` in the docs, such as on the ["Environment Variables" page](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/guides/env_vars.html?highlight=zephyr_base), so I'm not sure if these scripts are intended to still be used.

I might also issue a PR to the `west` repo to improve the error message when west is run outside of a workspace.

title: twister: BabbleSim support
body:
Adds BabbleSim support to Twister, allowing BabbleSim tests to be
defined using testcase.yaml. This adds a new bsim harness for Twister,
with 4 new options in the harness_config entry in testcase.yaml.

The new harness supports running any number of different testids in the
same application binary, along with a phy. Mixing different
applications is not supported, and it's not possible to pass arbitrary
arguments to the applications or the phy. Even with these limitations,
all BabbleSim tests defined under tests/bluetooth/bsim_bt are supported,
apart from the EDTT tests, which rely on an additional python script.

The tests are run like the console harness tests, except multiple
proceses are spawned in parallel, according to
harness_config.bsim_tests. The test pass/fail criteria is based on the
return code of the simulation processes the same way run_parallel.sh
does, and no regex is applied to the printed output.

BabbleSim tests can now be specified in testcase.yaml with the following
entries in harness_config:
- bsim_tests: List of BabbleSim tests to run in parallel, as a list of
  objects with parameters for each test.
- bsim_phy: Parameters for the BabbleSim Phy, including the name of the
  physical layer to run the tests.

All tests_scripts shell scripts (except EDTT) can now be replaced by
single test entries in testcase.yaml for each test application:

```yml
tests:
  bluetooth.test.id:
    harness: bsim
    platform_allow: nrf52_bsim
    harness_config:
      bsim_phy:
        name: bs_2G4_phy_v1
        sim_length: 20.0
      bsim_tests:
        - id: test_id_1
          real_encryption: true
          rs: 5
        - id: test_id_2
```
Replaces all bash scripts for the BabbleSim tests with testcase.yaml
entries, where possible. As the EDTT tests need a python script to run
in parallel, this has been left as-is, along with the framework scripts
required to run them.

title: Add CTE receive and sampling in Bluetooth stack
body:
The PR provides CTE receive and sampling functionality in BLE stack. It includes all three parts of implementation: controller, HCI, host.

The controller part: 
- Added changes in radio implementation to enable CTE reception for periodic advertising scan events.
- Added API to get information about antenna id used to measure RSSI.
- Added API to get CTEInfo PDU field parsed by radio peripheral.
- New noder_rx type introduced. Thanks to that we are able to manage memory for required collected IQ samples separately from memory for regular PDUs. The node_rx_iq_report has node_rx_hdr, so it may be processed by regular received nodes path up to HCI.
- Added enable or disable CTE receive in LL thread and ULL. The CTE enable and sampling configuration are provided to LLL via double buffer (stored in lll_sync). That functionality works in a similar way like double buffered PDUs in advertising role.
- Added handling of HCI_LE_Set_Connectionless_IQ_Sampling_Enable HCI command.
- Added dropping of unreported node_rx_iq_repots if CTE receive was disabled by Host in the meantime (e.g. disable operation was preempted by periodic advertising sync event and new node_rx_iq_report was put in receive path).
- Added unit tests for handling of HCI_LE_Set_Connectionless_IQ_Sampling_Enable.

The HCI part:
- Added HCI_LE_Set_Connectionless_IQ_Sampling_Enable command.
- Added HCI_LE_Connectionless_IQ_Report.

The host part:
- Added API to enable or disable CTE receive and sampling.
- Added API to register callbacks for IQ samples report receive.
- Added handling of HCI_LE_Connectionless_IQ_Report event.

The PR is long. I'm sorry for that. Splitting it at this stage (in my humble opinion) would increase the time it may be merged to master.

title: runners: nrfjprog: workaround for multi-core hex files
body:
The nrfjprog utility is not capable of flashing a hex file which
affects the flash memories of both coprocessors of the nRF53 family of
SoCs.

However, the user is capable of creating such a hex file using the
HEX_FILES_TO_MERGE build system variable.

An example use case is to build a bluetooth controller application for
the network core, then use the zephyr.hex file in that build directory
as the HEX_FILES_TO_MERGE argument for a separate Bluetooth
application build targeting the app core.

Work around this by detecting the situation and doing the right thing
by splitting the hex file back up again, even if thats a bit awkward.
Splitting the hex into app and network core components allows them to
be flashed separately. This is the only way we can get the job done
with nrfjprog.

This is arguably nicer since there's just one 'west flash' invocation.
At least in the use case named above, you wouldn't need to rebuild the
controller application very often, so this is a simpler user workflow.

When low power is enabled on the system and when going to sleep, the lptim counts and wakes up the kernel though its interrupt routine.
The soc policy decides to go to sleep, if compatible with its residency when calling the sys_pm_policy_next_state for a nb of kernel ticks.

This PR is requires the support of the LPTimer on stm32l5  #32999

Note that DEEP_SLEEP modes are not enabled yet, as LPTIM cannot run during stm32 standby or shutdown modes.

title: logging: File system backend
body:
This PR introduces a new LOG backend based on VFS API. It is able to store Loggs in multiple files in pointed log directory

* cold start supported
If FS volume is not mounted from the beginning the backend will drop LOG. Backend will start logging normally once FS volume will be mounted (so FS can be directly mounted by the application either). Obviously the backend works well especially if FS volume is automounted within zephyr-rtos startup.
* auto recovery after unexpected lost of the current log file in runtime.
If currently used log file is lost, the backend attempt to create another one.

On the first possible write attempt backend creates a new file with continuous numeration. When max size of file is reached. 
system creates another one. There is a limit of log files used by backend too. There is a possibility to overwrite
old files or drop new ones.


smp_svr sample was modifed so it has enabled FS commonest. This project could be used to test new backend.
The easiest way to download the log file is using this command:
mcumgr --conntype serial --connstring='dev=/dev/ttyACM0,baud=115200' fs download /lfs1/log.0000 ~/log.txt.

Wort to note that a Log file can be also read using FS shell.

This PR supersedes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/27486 as I took over the task and reworked base code much so want completely new review process.

title: Add support for setting function properties using Doxygen
body:
# Current approach
This PR is an attempt to resolve #21061 by using Doxygen aliases. Developer can add a list of function properties by using `@funcprops \prop1, ..., \propN`. They will be rendered as plain text in the Doxygen build and a with a link to terminology on the Sphinx side. Note that this solution does not allow to obtain a list of, e.g. "all functions that are async".

Doxygen output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110100647-ee3bc300-7da2-11eb-8be7-b24649fada22.png)

Sphinx output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110100680-f8f65800-7da2-11eb-9a66-0369a301e2f4.png)

**Pros**: Minimal changes, standardized keywords, renders links on the Sphinx side
**Cons**: Plain-text on the Doxygen side, not possible to list functions with a certain property

# Other options

## Links to terminology in both Doxygen and Sphinx
In order to achieve this functionality the `terminology.rst` content needs to be moved to a Doxygen page. Then, the `ALIAS` can contain, e.g. `@ref async`. The content of the Doxygen page can be rendered back in Sphinx using the recently added `..doxygenpage` directive in `breathe`, together with https://github.com/michaeljones/breathe/pull/645.

Doxygen output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110104742-d61a7280-7da7-11eb-8cbc-9ff018e7486e.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110104796-e4688e80-7da7-11eb-9b95-e6e6121b1964.png)

Sphinx output:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110104842-f3e7d780-7da7-11eb-9a76-e76c164f34f9.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110104886-02ce8a00-7da8-11eb-92bc-1c8516789eeb.png)

**Pros**: Function properties contain link to terminology in both, Doxygen and Sphinx.
**Cons**: Terminology has to be moved to Doxygen

# List of functions with a certain property

In order to obtain a list of functions that have a certain property, e.g. `async` I have tried the options listed below. Note that I haven't had success in obtaining a fully functional solution.

## `\xrefitem`
Using `\xrefitem <key> "(heading)" "(list title)" { text }` a new page is created in the Doxygen side with a list of all functions that have the property set. One of the problems is that the generated page is added to the root of the Doxygen tree. Furthermore, I haven't been able to make this option work reliably when multiple properties are used.

Doxygen:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110108534-9bff9f80-7dac-11eb-9921-84c5d004a4f0.png)

Sphinx:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110108494-8d18ed00-7dac-11eb-95b7-94dbbbfc52cd.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/110108451-7f636780-7dac-11eb-84e7-eca2659a8e56.png)

**Pros**: Pages with a list of all functions with a certain property are generated
**Cons**: **Not working properly on the Sphinx side** (renders empty), page location can't be controlled in the Doxygen side

## `\ingroup`
The advantage of using groups is that pages location can be controlled (e.g. creating a parent group somewhere in the hierarchy). However, the function will be listed in only one group, so it is not an option.

From Doxygen documentation:
> Note that compound entities (like classes, files and namespaces) can be put into multiple groups, but members (like variable, functions, typedefs and enums) can only be a member of one group (this restriction is in place to avoid ambiguous linking targets in case a member is not documented in the context of its class, namespace or file, but only visible as part of a group).

**Pros**: None
**Cons**: Does not work when multiple properties are used.

# Table of properties

In order to generate something like:

function           | syscall | reschedule | sleep | no-wait | isr-ok | pre-kernel-ok | async | supervisor
------------------ | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------- | ------ | ------------- | ----- | ----------
k_mutex_init       | YES     | no         | no    | yes     | yes    |               |       |
k_mutex_lock       | YES     | yes        | YES   | YES     | NO*    |               |       |

I haven't found a solution using existing Doxygen/Sphinx/Breathe facilities. On the Doxygen side we should have conditionals to evaluate certain properties of a function. As fas as I know, this is not possible. Onthe Sphinx side we need to implement  a new custom plugin that parses Doxygen XML files and generates such table. It may be possible to re-use `breathe` parser, but I'm not sure it it is worth for this purpose due to its "complexity".

* Add support of C++ RTTI
* Implements new and delete using k_malloc and k_free

title: doc: power management: Remove references to previous PM states terminology
body:
**Describe the bug**

Following merge of https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/31273
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/power_management/index.html was not updated.
Particularly the following terminology is not up to date anymore:
```
:dfn:`Active State`
   The CPU and clocks are powered on. This is the normal operating state when
   the system is running.

:dfn:`Sleep State`
   Some of the SoC clocks are gated. The CPU is stopped but does not lose
   execution context. Configuration of the peripherals is preserved.

:dfn:`Deep Sleep State`
   The SoC is power gated and loses context. Most peripherals would also be
   power gated. RAM may be selectively retained.

:dfn:`Idle Thread`
   A system thread that runs when there are no other threads ready to run.

:dfn:`Power gating`
   Power gating reduces power consumption by shutting off current to blocks of
   the integrated circuit that are not in use.
```


**To Reproduce**
See doc.

**Impact**
Confusion

title: settings: add support for eeprom storage
body:
Add the possibility to the settings subsystem to use eeprom storage. On the eeprom each name-value (id-value) entry is represented as a record containing:
```
------------------------------------------
| reclen | idmaxidx | id  | data | crc16 |
------------------------------------------
with:
	reclen: record length: (uint16_t)
	idmaxidx: length of id - 1: (uint8_t)
	id: id or name
	data: data or value
	crc16: calculated over id + data: (uint16_t)
```

These records are stored one after the other. Records are deleted by making the crc16 invalid. When there is no more place to write a new record a data compression routine is called to remove all deleted records from eeprom storage.

The proposed storage allows to specify a limited region of an eeprom as storage. The default however is to use the full eeprom0 area for storage.

title: fs: littlefs: fix default cache size
body:
Originally the file cache used a mem_pool, but that data structure has been deprecated and replaced by a heap that includes metadata in the  heap area.  As a result attempts to allocate all blocks will fail because some of the reservation intended for cache data is now holding metadata instead.
    
It's not immediately clear how to adjust the required heap size to support this metadata as it depends on heap chunk units and data structures that are not visible to the application.  Experimentally a value of 24 bytes works, while smaller values do not.
    
Further the previous Kconfig API to configure the allocation pool is completely inappropriate with the new heap data structure which has such different behavior.
    
So: Deprecate the old Kconfig API.  Add a new Kconfig option to directly control the cache size.  Infer a default cache size that works with the old mem_pool parameters assuming a per-block overhead.  But to avoid wasted memory use the heap allocation only when the application customizes the size, and use a slab in other cases.

Also refactor the tests so both default and custom allocations are tested, and the ability to allocate the maximum number of files and directories is also verified.

Fixes #31524

body:
This allows users to overrule a module from command line.
As example, the Zephyr build system loads the module FOO from
`modules/FOO`, but user has a custom FOO locally at `custom/FOO` and
would like to use this module instead of manifest specified.

If user does `-DZEPHYR_EXTRA_MODULES=custom/FOO` the following error
will be seen:
```
The binary directory

  build/modules/FOO

is already used to build a source directory.  It cannot be used to build
source directory

  custom/FOO

Specify a unique binary directory name.
```

Removing duplicates from the list allows a user to use
`-DZEPHYR_EXTRA_MODULES=custom/FOO` and thus replace `modules/FOO` for
the current build.

Synthesize a unique name from the node dependency ordinal instead, and update the gen_defines script to record the name associated with the full path in the extern declaration.

Also update the ethernet device DTS helper function to use the same inference for dev_name and label that the real one does, since it bypasses the real one.

title: Logging: Overhaul
body:
Logging v2 highlights
----------------------------
- `log_strdup` no longer needed!!
- logging `long long`, `float` and `double` is now possible!!
- hex dumps with formatted strings
- Self-contained messages (even transient strings are there)
- 32/64 bit timestamp
- better memory utilization - ~20% more messages fit in the logging buffer
- 6x faster logging from userspace!
- overall simplified implementation

API changes
-----------------
No change in logging API! Add `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFFERED=y` to run sample with new version. Only backend API extended with a function for processing v2 messages. PR updates following backends to support v2:
- uart
- shell
- adsp
- rtt
- native_posix

To be added later: bluetooth monitor, net, spinel, swo, xtensa sim

Internals
------------
It is utilizing cbprintf packages (#30675, #31102) to create self-contained log message. Using `_Generic` feature of C11, it is possible to act based on types of arguments. It is used to determine when formatted string requires time consuming, runtime package creation and when log message can be created as simple serialization of the arguments. When  `char *` arguments are present in the log message then package is created at runtime. This includes copying into a message any string argument which is from rw memory.

Additionally, log messages are no longer stored as fragmented chunks allocated from a memslab. They are stored in a circular buffer. This ensures that log message is not fragmented and improves memory utilization. Circular buffer is somehow generic multi producer, single consumer packet buffer (`lib/os/mpsc_pbuf`). Additional requirement is to support overwrite mode where oldest packets are dropped when new message cannot be allocated. MPSC packet buffer uses alloc, commit, claim, free sequence to avoid copying. Additionally, it has functions optimized for storing single word and single word + pointer packets. It is forseen that those will be used by the tracing to logger functionality.

It pends currently on #33567 being solved. PR contains temporary workaround to get CI green.

PR content
---------------
- mpsc packet buffer
- new log_msg2 implementation
- adaptation of the logger to support both version
- adaptation of  some logger backends to support v2 api

Fixes #26170
Fixes #18351
Fixes #26246
Fixes #30353

title: Bluetooth: host: Prevent calls to bt_rand before bt_enable
body:
Prevent the bt_rand function from being called before bt_enable.
Depending on the implementation of bt_rand this function cannot
be called before bluetooth has been initialized. With host supplied
crypto functions the HCI LE rand command is used for example.

The use case for calling bt_id_create before bt_enable is meant for
when the application has storage for the identity instead of the stack.
So we add the requirement that the application has to have storage
for the identity resolving key (IRK) in addition when the local
device is privacy-enabled.

Deprecate the bt_set_id_addr API function. This is merely a wrapper
for the bt_id_create function now, except an IRK cannot be given.
When CONFIG_BT_PRIVACY is enabled an IRK has to be given by the
application because the bt_rand function cannot be called before
bt_enable.

title: Implement null-pointer de-referencing detection for Cortex-M
body:
Fixes #3634 


- The PR implements null-pointer dereferencing (R/W) detection for Cortex-M architecture
    - using the DWT peripheral where available
    - using the MPU peripheral when DWT is not available
- It is recommended (and implemented) as a **debug feature only**: enabling null-pointer detection will:
    - increase flash footprint, as it will un-map some area starting from address 0x0 (1kB by default)
    - reserve 1 or 2 DWT comparator(s), depending on the architecture variant, or,
    - consume 1 MPU region, if DWT is not used/present.
- Null pointer exception detection is _enforced_ in the entire test tree, to be able to catch accidental null pointer dereferencing in our tests
- It is emulated and verified in QEMU (mps2_an385).

The feature is not recommended in production code.
The feature is useful for privileged threads/ ISRs, which normally have access to all flash / sram 
It's also useful for user threads, as normally reading flash area is allowed in nPRIV mode.

The feature is implemented based on the same principle as the solution for x86 (see #3634)

- Missing/Future-work
    - documentation [release note entry is now added] of the feature
    - possibly a new error code specific to null-pointer exception (e.g. K_ERROR_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION) (CC @andrewboie)

title: net: coap: Rework packet retransmission concept
body:
* **Rework pending retransmission logic**

    Introduce retransmission counter to the coap_pending structure. This allows to simplify the retransmission logic and allows to keep track of the number of remaining retranmissions.
  
    Additionally, extend the `coap_pending_init()` function with `retries` parameter, which allows to set the retransmission count individually for each confirmable transaction.
  
    Fixes #28117

* **Randomize initial ACK timeout** 

    Add Kconfig option to randomize the initial ACK timeout, as specified in RFC 7252. The option is enabled by default.

    Additionally, finetune the default value of COAP_INIT_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS option, to match the default ACK_TIMEOUT value specified by the RFC 7252. The RFC does not specify the minimum/maximum value of the ACK_TIMEOUT parameter, but only suggests it should be no lower than 1 second, so adjust the option range to reflect this.

title: doc: module naming rule in zephyr/module.yml
body:
Introducing `name: <module-name>` as requirement in Zephyr maintained
modules.

This will ensure that Zephyr module names are kept in sync between the
project names in the default `west.yml` manifest file, and the names
used when referring to the Zephyr module in the build system.

This means the project `foo` in `west.yml` will look as:

west.yml
```
manifest:
  projects:
    - name: foo
```

must have:
`<foo-repo>/zephyr/module.yml` with content
```
name: foo
```

and can be referred to in the build system as:
- `ZEPHYR_FOO_MODULE_DIR`, for the module directory
- `ZEPHYR_FOO_CMAKE_DIR`, for the directory containing the Zephyr module
  CMakeLists.txt.

Signed-off-by: Torsten Rasmussen <Torsten.Rasmussen@nordicsemi.no>


--------

title: scripts: module: support for name field in zephyr/module.yml
body:
The folder name of a Zephyr module is also used as its module name
when integrating it into the build system.

This means that a Zephyr module, BAR, located in:
```
<workspace>/modules/foo
                    |--- zephyr
                          |--- CMakeLists.txt
                          |--- Kconfig
```

will be referred to as FOO in the build system, that is:
ZEPHYR_FOO_MODULE_DIR==<workspace>/modules/foo
ZEPHYR_FOO_CMAKE_DIR==<workspace>/modules/foo/zephyr

The `name` field allows the module to specify its module name,
independent of its location like:

`<workspace>/modules/foo/zephyr/module.yml`
```
name: bar
build:
  cmake: zephyr
```

will instead be referred to as BAR in the build system, that is:
ZEPHYR_BAR_MODULE_DIR==<workspace>/modules/foo
ZEPHYR_BAR_CMAKE_DIR==<workspace>/modules/foo/zephyr

This allows for greater flexibility of relocating Zephyr modules in
other folders and at the same time be guaranteed that other modules
depending on `ZEPHYR_BAR_MODULE_DIR` is still working.

If `name` field is not specified in `module.yml`, then the existing
behavior of using the folder name will be used.

-------

Introducing `name: <module-name>` as requirement in Zephyr maintained
modules.

This will ensure that Zephyr module names are kept in sync between the
project names in the default `west.yml` manifest file, and the names
used when referring to the Zephyr module in the build system.

This means the project `foo` in `west.yml` will look as:

west.yml
```
manifest:
  projects:
    - name: foo
```

must have:
`<foo-repo>/zephyr/module.yml` with content
```
name: foo
```

and can be referred to in the build system as:
- `ZEPHYR_FOO_MODULE_DIR`, for the module directory
- `ZEPHYR_FOO_CMAKE_DIR`, for the directory containing the Zephyr module
  CMakeLists.txt.

title: doc: improve west's repo-tool.rst
body:
Various improvements to the west repo-tool.rst page and pages that
link to it:

Rename the page title to "Basics", since it documents, well the
basics, including built-in commands like "help" an "config" that are
not directly related to multiple repositories.

The "multi-repo" term was invented before we started using
"workspace". Drop it from the text and rework things using words like
"workspace", "basics", or "built-ins" instead, which read better.

We've been using west for a long enough time that justifying its
existence prominently at the start of this page is no longer
necessary; move that to the "dustbin of history" page (why.rst).

Try harder to clarify exactly what a "project" is, along with other
workspace related clarifications.

Improve the documentation for the west init and west update commands,
and create :ref: targets for linking directly to them for convenience
elsewhere in the docs.

Slim down the usages for other built-in commands, so we don't have to
keep those up to date as carefully each release. This is about to be
important for west 0.9, which is going to change the detailed
semantics for the "[PROJECT ...]" part of each command synopsis in a
way that will be inconvenient to duplicate for each of these.

Move the "Topologies supported" content lower down. Try to help the
reading flow by letting people get familiar with a workspace and what
you can do with it using the Zephyr GSG workspace that they probably
already have before overwhelming them with other possibilities and
choices.

title: bt: ipc: Add ipc multiendpoint
body:
Multiprotocol on the nRF53 requires multiple IPC channels to communicate
between the APP and the NET core. One way is to duplicate the entire openamp
instance, the other one is to use a single instance with multiple endpoints.

Aim of this PR is to achieve the goal using the simpler single instance
with the multiple endpoints.

At this point hci_rpmsg net core sample and peripheral_hr app core sample link with the new implementation.

To build:
```
cd ncs/zephyr/samples/bluetooth/hci_rpmsg
west build -b nrf5340dk_nrf5340_cpunet -- -DCONF_FILE="prj.conf overlay-multiendpoint-ipc.conf"

cd ncs/zephyr/samples/bluetooth/peripheral_hr
west build -b nrf5340dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -- -DCONF_FILE="prj.conf overlay-multiendpoint-ipc.conf"
```

For now we are aware of the following issues that may need addressing:

title: linker: generate memory regions from devicetree partitions
body:
Implements a relatively simple mechanism for automatically generating memory regions based devicetree partitions.
For a partition to result in a memory region, it must add the `linker-region` property to the appropriate partition.
Only partitions under the `chosen/zephyr,flash` node result in memory regions, under the assumption that this points at the onboard ROM, and that memory regions for external flash do not make sense.
Regions are named based on the label of the partition.

The primary purpose of this PR is to enable placing constants at absolute addresses in a portable manner.

Naming for `FOR_EACH_NESTED` and `linker-region` is provisional pending feedback.
Currently this has only been integrated into the Cortex linker script and enabled on a small subset of nRF hardware.

Implements #31073
